title: Proactive Physical AI through Continuous Observation and Timely Intervention
abstract: Physical AI is commonly formulated around an explicitly specified task: given a goal or instruction, a system perceives, reasons, and acts. In many real-world settings, however, important tasks emerge from continuously changing world states before a person explicitly formulates them. We study this complementary problem as Proactive Physical AI, where an AI system continuously observes the physical world, identifies situations that warrant intervention, and initiates appropriate actions at the right time. We develop ProAgent, an end-to-end system built around two components: a Jev-style proactive timing model (dubbed StreamingJev) that determines whether and when intervention is needed, and a Response Model that generates responses for people or invokes available device capabilities for physical execution. To support learning at scale, we develop an automated data pipeline that converts videos into supervision for proactive timing. Experiments demonstrate strong proactive performance under both explicit objectives and standing roles, combining more accurate intervention timing with fewer false triggers than the source-backbone baseline. Real-robot evaluations further demonstrate ProAgent's ability to identify emerging needs and translate them into appropriate physical actions.

title: Universal Distributed Feature Extraction Complementary to Side Information via H-Score
abstract: This paper considers a distributed estimation system where edge nodes transmit averaged features to a center node for parameter estimation. A key challenge arises when the center node possesses auxiliary side information: how to design local extractors that are universally optimal for any downstream task, while avoiding redundancy with the side information. To tackle this problem, we orthogonally decompose the joint function space and demonstrate in the weak-dependence regime that the modal decomposition of the canonical dependence kernel's conditional-additive component yields optimal, task-independent features. We construct a distributed nested H-score to learn this decomposition and show that, under a limited feature budget, the mean-squared error (MSE) gap to the best task-specific features is determined solely by the task's alignment with the discarded, least informative modes, and vanishes to leading order for every square-integrable task once the budget is sufficient.

title: On error bounds and noncritical Lagrange multipliers
abstract: Critical Lagrange multipliers are known to be responsible for the potentially slow convergence of Newton-type methods, and noncriticality of a given multiplier has been tied to an error bound which estimates the distance of a primal-dual pair associated with a perturbed problem to the primal solution and the multiplier set of the unperturbed one, and is decisive for a local convergence analysis. We investigate this relation in an abstract setting where merely a set-valued mapping assigning primal-dual pairs to a parameter is available, and characterize the error bound of interest in terms of noncriticality of the underlying multiplier and two calmness-type properties of the associated multiplier mapping, one of which is a novel weak inner calmness in the fuzzy sense. No structural assumptions on the underlying problem are needed for that, and the two calmness-type conditions are not only sufficient but also necessary. Afterwards, we specify these findings for composite optimization problems. Whenever the subdifferential of the outer function is a polyhedral mapping, both conditions hold automatically, which explains the equivalence of noncriticality and the error bound observed in the polyhedral setting. Whenever the outer function is C^2-decomposable, they are secured by calmness of a restricted multiplier mapping together with a closedness condition, which recovers and extends the known characterization for C^2-cone reducible constraint systems.

title: AI-Powered Adaptive Learning and Smart Education Platform
abstract: Education is becoming increasingly digital, yet many students still face difficulties in understanding complex concepts, remembering long answers, identifying their learning gaps, and preparing effectively for examinations. This paper presents an AI-powered adaptive learning platform designed to provide personalized and interactive learning support. The system uses Artificial Intelligence to explain questions in detail, generate short exam-oriented answers and recall keywords, analyze students' performance, identify knowledge gaps, and recommend suitable learning tasks. The platform also provides 3D visualization for mathematical and geometric concepts, AI-assisted learning for languages such as Marathi and Sanskrit with Hindi and English explanations, AI-based viva examination, instant tests, PDF/notes-based learning, progress tracking, and gamification. The main aim is to make learning personalized, understandable, interactive, and focused on actual student improvement rather than simply providing answers

title: Outlier Detection for Shale Gas Production Data: An Integrated Approach of Enhanced Clustering and Domain Knowledge
abstract: Abstract Shale gas production data are inherently non-stationary, characterized by distinct decline trends across various production stages. These datasets are frequently contaminated with outliers stemming from operational interventions, such as well shut-ins and choke adjustments, as well as sensor malfunctions and human-induced collection errors. Consequently, robust outlier detection is a prerequisite for reliable production data analysis. While unsupervised learning algorithms, such as Local Outlier Factor (LOF), Angle-Based Outlier Detection (ABOD), and Isolation Forest (IF), are currently employed, their efficacy is often hindered by the subjectivity involved in defining manual thresholds for anomaly partitioning. This study develops an enhanced unsupervised classification algorithm, termed IF-K-Medoids, by integrating the IF algorithm with K-Medoids clustering. This hybrid algorithm addresses the initialization sensitivity of K-Medoids by leveraging IF to optimally select initial cluster centers, thereby eliminating the need for random or manual selection. Furthermore, the K-Medoids enables automated differentiation between anomalous and normal samples, overcoming the subjectivity of manual thresholding. This algorithm is then incorporated into a two-stage outlier detection approach that fuses machine learning with domain knowledge. IF-K-Medoids performs an initial screening of outliers, which are then further reviewed using domain knowledge. This two-stage outlier detection approach enhances both the accuracy and reliability of identifying outliers in production data. The IF-K-Medoids algorithm was first validated using datasets from the University of California-Irvine (UCI) Machine Learning Repository, achieving an Area Under the Curve (AUC) exceeding 0.88, which outperforms standalone IF and Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) algorithms. The proposed two-stage outlier detection approach was subsequently validated using field data from two shale gas wells. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach produced physically interpretable detection results, thereby facilitating improvements in the accuracy and precision of production forecasting, reserves estimation, and rate transient analysis for shale gas wells.

title: LimAgents: Multi-Agent LLMs for Generating Research Limitations
abstract: Identifying scientific limitations is essential for transparent reporting and rigorous critical appraisal. However, zero-shot large language models (LLMs) often produce generic critiques, repeat author-stated limitations, and overlook paper-specific methodological and contextual weaknesses. We propose LimAgents, a training-free multi-agent framework in which role-specialized workers extract explicit limitations, analyze methodological weaknesses, adopt a peer-review perspective, and examine cited literature. Workers can refine their outputs through feedback from a Leader Agent, after which a Master Agent consolidates and de-duplicates the resulting limitations; ablations show that refinement benefits GPT-4o mini but not Llama 3 8B. For evaluation, we construct a validated, non-exhaustive reference set by combining author-stated limitations with OpenReview critiques and decomposing them into atomic Limitation Units through multi-model consensus. We evaluate generated limitations using human-calibrated, LU-level semantic matching with two independent LLM judges. Across multiple backbones, LimAgents achieves the highest F1 across both baseline-comparison backbones. In terms of reference-aligned coverage, it achieves improvements of 4.41 and 15.51 points over the Llama 3 8B and GPT-4o mini zero-shot configurations, respectively. Furthermore, LimAgents yields substantial gains in overall F1 scores, exceeding competing baselines by 12.30–20.91 points when utilizing Mistral 7B, and 5.31–34.18 points with Qwen 2.5 3B. Code: https://github.com/IbrahimAlAzhar/LimAgents_limitation_generation_with_LLM_Agents | Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/IbrahimAlAzhar/LimAgents

title: Multimodal spatiotemporal knowledge graph construction for conflict-event analysis: an integrated framework with geographic entity-map association
abstract: Heterogeneous conflict-event information is distributed across textual reports, web images, and scanned maps, making it difficult to represent entities, events, geographic locations, temporal attributes, and multimedia evidence within a unified knowledge graph. This study proposes an integrated framework for constructing multimodal spatiotemporal knowledge graphs from event-oriented heterogeneous data. The framework combines textual entity, relation, and event extraction; visual object detection; scanned-map coordinate recognition; geographic entity grounding; cross-modal entity fusion; provenance-aware storage; and graph visualization. A cascaded YOLOv5-PaddleOCR procedure first detects and crops coordinate annotation regions from scanned maps and then reconstructs the map extent from the recognized coordinates. Textual place entities are geocoded using GeoNames and linked to relevant maps through point-polygon spatial intersection. Quantitative experiments showed F1-scores of 0.76-0.84 for the evaluated text extraction tasks. For aircraft, ship, and general web-image detection, YOLOv8 obtained mAP@0.5 values of 0.935, 0.890, and 0.922, respectively. On the 287-map scanned-map dataset, YOLOv5 achieved a region-detection F1-score of 0.977. In the 278-map paired out-of-fold OCR evaluation, complete map-coordinate recognition increased from 64.03% with direct PaddleOCR to 87.05% with the cascaded procedure, and the paired difference was statistically significant (exact McNemar test, p < 0.001). Under an event- and source-document-grouped evaluation protocol, the complete constrained cross-modal entity-fusion method achieved an F1-score of 0.884. A conflict-event case study further demonstrates the practical applicability of the framework.

title: TorchSpin: Differentiable Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Simulation in PyTorch
abstract: Interpreting electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectra commonly requires repeated forward simulation and optimization of spin Hamiltonian parameters. Established software provides mature simulation and fitting methods, but these calculations are not generally available as differentiable components within machine-learning workflows. We present TorchSpin, an open-source PyTorch framework that ports the organization and numerical conventions of EasySpin into a tensor-based computational environment. title: CodeLift: Your Test Suite Is Secretly a Dense SWE Curriculum
abstract: The pass-all-test binary reward has become a standard recipe for training software engineering agents, but its sparsity eliminates difference of partially correct patches. The test pass-rate is a natural alternative. However, we find that it is not a reliable indicator of patch quality. A functionality being tested can be covered by either one challenging test or one hundred trivial tests, where the majority might be already satisfied pass-to-pass tests. We introduce CodeLift, a reinforcement learning method that dynamically calibrates pass-rate rewards, turning the test suite into an adaptive curriculum. At each iteration, CodeLift groups tests that kill the same patches and patches that pass the same tests, then gives more weight to test groups that fewer patch groups pass. This reduces the impact of majority simple tests and focuses more on what is still challenging. Within each rollout, CodeLift applies the same scoring rule to repository snapshots, assigning credit to useful actions even when later ones introduce regressions. Experiments on SWE benchmarks show that CodeLift consistently improves pass@1/2/4/8 over binary and pass-rate baselines. Analyses show that CodeLift provides dense, stable learning signals and unlocks the inherent curriculum in the test suite.

title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part I: Glauber Dynamics
abstract: In the tensor principal components analysis (tensor PCA) problem, we are asked to recover an unknown vector in $\{\pm1\}^N$ from a noisy observation of its $k$-th tensor power, for a fixed $k\ge3$. Tensor PCA exhibits a well-studied information-computation gap: global algorithms such as spectral methods and sum-of-squares work above an algorithmic threshold, below which we know matching lower bounds (against these and some other restricted models of computation). In contrast, local algorithms such as Markov chains were only known to succeed from a random initialization at a polynomially larger signal-to-noise ratio, and were believed to be inferior to global algorithms for tensor PCA. We show that Glauber dynamics, when supplemented with annealing and ergodic averaging, achieves polynomial-time strong recovery above the algorithmic threshold from a uniformly random initialization, demonstrating that local Markov chains can succeed all the way down to the algorithmic threshold from an uninformative cold start.

title: DIGS: Distribution-Informed Gaussian Splatting for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation
abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D Gaussian segmentation typically binds semantic features to the per-Gaussian state via per-scene gradient training (1-4 h) or the more recent closed-form distillation. Both commit each primitive to a single feature; therefore, boundary Gaussians spanning multiple 2D instances are forced into a hard decision that degrades retrieval accuracy and yields unstable mask boundaries at render time. We present DIGS, a training-free framework with two stages, class-agnostic mapping and multi-modal encoding, that decouples instance discovery from linguistic naming. At the Gaussian level, our distribution-informed representation maintains an explicit top-$M$ label distribution per primitive, updated by a tempered Dirichlet rule; preservation of multi-peaked label distributions at boundary primitives allows a late-argmax renderer to recover clean instance boundaries. A bidirectional state machine aggregates these distributions into a persistent class-agnostic instance ontology. The instance-level encoding stage then fuses the CLIP visual embedding of each instance's isolated 3D footprint with the CLIP-text embedding of an LLM-generated attribute description, disambiguating visually similar instances. On a single A100, DIGS completes mapping and instance encoding on LERF-OVS in 1.0-3.2 min per scene, depending on whether LLM fusion is enabled, and serves native 3D queries in 5.4 ms. It reaches 71.95% mean mIoU on LERF-OVS, outperforming both the training-free SFS and training-based LaGa baselines. DIGS also achieves the highest mean mIoU on LERF-Mask and 3D-OVS and surpasses Gaga and ObjectGS on Replica under their respective evaluation protocols. Code is available at https://github.com/ZephyrZos/DIGS.

title: Confidential Error-Correcting Codes
abstract: We introduce Confidential Error-correcting Codes (CECs), a new cryptographic primitive that enables reliable decoding from perturbed codewords while preserving message confidentiality. We formalize this primitive through three security properties: confidentiality, robustness, and soundness. To realize this goal, we develop a general framework for constructing CECs based on a Randomness-Security Separation (RSS) structure, which first encodes a nonce to introduce randomness and then masks the encoded payload with a pseudorandom function. Based on our RSS framework, we instantiate CECs, called Conc-CEC, using concatenated Reed-Muller and Reed-Solomon codes. The resulting Conc-CEC admits provable guarantees for all three properties. Notably, compared to PRCs (CRYPTO'24), another recent cryptographic primitive with error-correcting capability, CECs achieve significantly stronger concrete security guarantees under practical parameter settings. As a primary application of CECs, we further present CECMark, a watermarking scheme for AI-generated images. Our experiments on real-world generative image models show that CECMark consistently outperforms state-of-the-art watermarking methods, including Gaussian Shading (CVPR'24), PRCMark (ICLR'25), and T2SMark (NeurIPS'25). In particular, CECMark achieves higher robustness across all 56 evaluated perturbations and ensures a false positive rate below $10^{-5}$ without introducing side effects. Taken together, our work lays a novel cryptographic foundation for trustworthy watermarking schemes that, for the first time, unify provable security guarantees with strong practical reliability.

title: Scalar Perturbations and Induced Gravitational Waves from First-Order Phase Transitions in Lattice Simulations
abstract: Cosmological first-order phase transitions can generate curvature perturbations through inhomogeneous quantum tunneling, as studied previously on superhorizon scales. In this work, we for the first time conduct three-dimensional lattice simulations that incorporate scalar metric perturbations and radiation perturbations, covering a range from bubble wall scales to super-horizon scales. We obtain the precise scalar perturbation power spectrum and the probability density function of energy density perturbations. Furthermore, we simulate the gravitational-wave energy spectra generated by each source during the first-order phase transition, including the scalar field itself, scalar metric perturbations, and the energy density and velocity perturbations of radiation. For gravitational waves, the contribution from other sources can exceed 1/3 of that from the scalar field at superhorizon scales. Additionally, we compare the effects of different values of the transition strength and rate on the results. This paper provides more accurate numerical results for research aimed at detecting or constraining first-order phase transitions via gravitational waves and curvature perturbations.

title: CLEAR-FORCE: A reservoir computing framework for closed-loop brain stimulation
abstract: Abstract Electrical stimulation of brain activity has emerged as a key therapeutic intervention for neurological diseases. The success of these approaches relies on precisely tuned stimulation parameters. A major challenge is that these parameters should ideally be adjusted in real-time based on changes in brain activity. Closed-loop controllers address this challenge by monitoring brain activity and adapting stimulation according to ongoing changes in neural dynamics. While machine learning has been helpful in this context, closed-loop controllers typically do not adapt in real-time to fluctuations in brain activity. Here, we propose a novel framework based on reservoir computing to train a closed-loop, real-time neural controller. This approach, termed CLEAR-FORCE, trains the output weights of a recurrent network based on a combination of target signals and feedback from brain activity. Two series of simulations were performed, where the controller was successful at (1) inducing neural oscillations in a population of spiking neurons and (2) suppressing pathological oscillations. This framework provides a promising avenue for the implementation of neural controllers in low-powered, real-time, and adaptive hardware that harnesses machine learning for the personalized treatment of brain disorders.

title: NLP-Based Student Readability Assessment and Personalized Feedback System
abstract: Student writing assessment is important in academic learning, but manual evaluation of written responses can require considerable time and may provide limited information about specific writing difficulties. This paper presents an NLP-Based Student Readability Assessment and Personalized Feedback System for automated analysis of student English writing. The system allows users to enter text directly or upload PDF, DOCX, and TXT documents. Submitted content is analyzed for readability, grammar, spelling, vocabulary, sentence structure, and text statistics. Seven readability measures are used to estimate reading difficulty, while vocabulary richness, repeated words, difficult words, sentence length, and sentence type provide additional writing characteristics. The system combines these results to generate an overall writing-quality score and a feature-weighted proficiency estimate. Personalized suggestions explain detected weaknesses and recommend areas for improvement. Teacher-managed assignments with reference answers and student submissions are also supported. Analysis records are stored per user in a lightweight database.

title: TSI-CORE-1.0-RC2: supporting repository and verification files
abstract: TSI-CORE 1.0-RC2 — Public Research Release Candidate Author: Igor Chechelnitsky ORCID: 0009-0007-4607-1946 Project: Theory of Structural Invariants (TSI-CORE) Original specification date: 30 July 2026 Release status: Public preprint candidate for independent scientific review. Overview TSI-CORE introduces a minimal formal kernel for representations and partial transformations, formulated in classical many-sorted first-order logic with equality. The specification addresses structural equivalence, partial action, declared composition, and a distinguished unit transformation through six mandatory axiom groups. The mathematical kernel deliberately does not assume physical reality, consciousness, time, dynamics, probability, memory, or any particular computational implementation. Included editions Four complementary reading editions are provided: Scientific specification — English (normative mathematical source) Scientific exposition — Russian Accessible explanation — English Accessible explanation — Russian The repository additionally includes the canonical RC2 specification, historical audit materials, finite-model verification scripts, reference outputs, and checksums. Verification and limitations Eight explicitly constructed finite examples have passed the included automated checker, covering the minimal model, axiom-independence witnesses, and an optional structural-preservation counterexample. These checks do not constitute complete machine-verified proofs, experimental validation, or independent peer review. Independent UTS audit The release also invites independent assessment of potential relationships between TSI and the UTS architecture. The audit investigates whether specific UTS mechanisms can be faithfully interpreted as extensions of TSI-CORE. Security properties involving consensus, concurrency, nullifiers, DAG ancestry, privacy, and bridge atomicity require independent assumptions and verification. No claim of UTS correctness is implied by the existence of TSI-CORE. Research integrity This release is a frozen public research candidate. Mathematical corrections must be documented and versioned rather than silently modifying the normative specification. Independent counterexamples, formalization attempts, references to prior work, and reproducible critical evaluations are welcome. Repository: https://github.com/Muhomor2/TSI-CORE Zenodo DOI: Pending archival registration. License: To be explicitly selected by the author before final publication.

title: A Speech-to-Knowledge Framework for Archaic Thai Language Understanding and Knowledge Graph Construction
abstract: Digitizing oral cultural heritage necessitates computational methods capable of bridging the acoustic, orthographic, and semantic gaps between historical and contemporary language forms. This study proposes a cascaded Automatic Speech Recognition–Neural Machine Translation–Knowledge Graph (ASR–NMT–KG) framework designed to transcribe archaic Thai recitations, translate them into modern Thai, and subsequently convert their semantic content into structured knowledge. The framework was evaluated utilizing the Thai Ancient Medical Speech Corpus (TAMSC), which comprises 14000 original and augmented utterances from ten certified Thai Traditional Medicine practitioners. The domain-adapted ASR model achieved a word error rate (WER) of 8.3%, a character error rate (CER) of 4.8%, and an Archaic Orthography Error Rate (AOER) of 6.2%. The mT5-Large translation model obtained a BLEU score of 51.7, while the Knowledge Graph construction module achieved an F1-score of 0.89. Furthermore, the WER exhibited a strong negative association with translation quality (Pearson’s r = −0.87, p < 0.001), providing empirical evidence of cross-stage performance dependency within the cascaded pipeline. These results indicate that the cascaded architecture offers an accurate, modular, and interpretable approach for preserving and semantically exploring low-resource historical language materials.

title: HATA: Multi-Agent Ontology Framework for High-Quality Log Interpretation Data Reconstruct in Existed Wells Re-Assessment
abstract: Abstract This study addresses the challenge of re-evaluating existed CNPC wells, where considerable potentials remain underestimated due to historical technological limitations and inconsistent interpretation workflows. In resources-scarce regions, existed well reassessment is essential for resource optimisation and supports the digital transformation of wells lifecycle management. This process relies on multi-modal data integration, including logs, interpretation charts, expert knowledge, and historical data, however, data inconsistencies, incompleteness, and semantic heterogeneity reduce analytical accuracy and impede value creation from data. To overcome these barriers, we propose an ontology-driven, multi-agent allied framework that autonomously re-constructs unified, high-quality datasets. The framework enables standardised data acquisition, intelligent quality control, missing-data and knowledge interpolation, and automated log processing, ensuring reliable and interpretable data supply throughout the re-assessment workflow among existed wells re-evaluation. We introduce the Human and Entity-centric Agent Travelling based Ontology Constructing (HATA) approach, an ontology based methodology aligned with knowledge management and intelligent system development. HATA employs a multi-agent architecture with 3 roles: the planner for task planning and orchestration, the traveller for ontology network construction through latent space "travelling," and the supervisor for validation and refinement. Agents first generate 3 most-possbile candidate ontology networks through digital-twin-based hypothesis testing, supported by data mining and data semantic management techniques. After agentic travelling to select optimal ontology, the system extracts log data, performs structural and semantic quality checks, interpolates missing values and link expert knowledge gaps, and executes log evaluation tasks. The outcomes guide iterative ontology refinement. Human-in-loop (HIL) interactions are supported through natural language and multi modal interfaces, enabling controllability and transparent reasoning consistent with engineering intent. Validation on 10 CNPC existed wells evaluated semantic understanding, task planning, ontology accuracy, data consistency, missing data interpolation, and reasoning completeness. Engineers assessed outputs using α ≥0.80 semantic similarity threshold across 3 interaction levels: Low (1–15 rounds), Mild (15–30), and High (30+). Intent comprehension and planning precision improved with interaction depth, demonstrating adaptive learning. More accurate ontology modelling strengthened fault tolerance for data compensation and hypothetical reasoning, though expert oversight remained essential for edge cases. Overall reasoning completeness, defined as ≥75% content judged reasonable, increased from 6 wells (Low) to 9 wells (High), confirming HATA's effectiveness as a controllable, interpretable assistant and its potential for deployment as an emerging technology in field operations. The results conclude that the manuscript presents a novel multi-agent framework for dynamic ontology modelling and automated dataset reconstructing tailored to existed well reassessment. By integrating role-specific agents, genAI, and ontology, the approach offers scalable, fault tolerant, and interpretable knowledge management. Its capabilities in task planning, iterative refinement, and "reasonable imagination" support reliable decision making and contribute directly to upstream digitalisation and emerging technology valuation. The methodology is believed extensible to other complex oilfield operations, providing a practical pathway for digital asset lifecycle enhancement.

title: Structure-preserving fidelity diagnostics for partial differential equations
abstract: Machine learning surrogates of partial differential equations (PDEs) are commonly trained on data generated by numerical solvers. Therefore, the training data obey not the PDE but the modified equation of the numerical scheme, and the test loss, computed on data from the same solver, cannot distinguish a model that learned the physics from one that learned the discretization error. Here, we show that the difference is nevertheless visible in the trained model. We propose a suite of structure-preserving fidelity diagnostics, simple scores that measure whether a learned model respects one known property of the physics, such as a conserved quantity, a symmetry or a Hamiltonian structure, without access to the training data or the governing equation. Over five systems, the diagnostics track the error with respect to the true dynamics with a rank correlation of up to $0.94$, while the test loss is uncorrelated or anti-correlated with it. For the Burgers, Korteweg-de Vries and Navier-Stokes equations, the diagnostics separate numerical schemes that the test loss ranks as equivalent, including schemes of the same order. order.

title: Compute-optimal data scaling for neural surrogates via multi-fidelity training
abstract: Neural surrogates for Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) are usually trained on synthetic data from numerical simulators. As models grow and scaling laws demand larger datasets, the cost of data generation often outweighs the training cost and becomes the bottleneck in the scaling quest. Unlike data in other domains, however, each PDE sample has a tunable cost that depends on its numerical fidelity, with the resulting cost-accuracy trade-off governed by known convergence rates. We exploit this property by formalizing neural surrogate training as a function of both data quantity and fidelity under a fixed data generation compute budget, treating fidelity as a fine-grained discrete spectrum rather than a binary distinction. Building on this, we show that multi-fidelity training enables Pareto-optimal error scaling against data generation compute. By using simulations at lower fidelities as an additional training signal, training on the optimal fidelity mixture matches the accuracy of high-fidelity-only training, with up to $6.3\times$ less data generation compute across our settings. We validate these findings across six PDE problems spanning structured grids and unstructured meshes, two distinct error sources (discretization and iterative-solver error), and four surrogate architectures, totaling over 7,000 training runs.

title: DiTSG: Context-Aware Air Traffic Scene Generation with Multi-Agent Diffusion Transformers
abstract: Understanding how many aircraft, and which traffic configurations, can be safely and efficiently managed by air traffic controllers within a given airspace is fundamental to air traffic management. Air traffic controllers continuously modify aircraft trajectories through interventions such as speed advisories and radar vectoring, and the patterns of these interventions are difficult to capture effectively using existing air traffic simulators. To address this limitation, we propose Diffusion Transformers for Traffic Scene Generation (DiTSG), which learns to generate air traffic scenes from recorded multi-aircraft trajectories. DiTSG employs stacked multi-agent inverted Transformer layers as the denoising backbone of a diffusion transformer, jointly generates the trajectories of multiple aircraft within a traffic scene, and conditions the generation on agent-specific required times of arrival. The resulting trajectories generated by DiTSG preserve realistic inter-aircraft interactions observed in actual air traffic operations. Experiments show that the DiTSG generates diverse traffic scenes that reproduce the statistical properties of recorded traffic while preserving realistic inter-aircraft interactions.

title: CryptoFlowBench: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Reasoning on Blockchains for Cryptocurrency Fund Tracing
abstract: Pseudonymous accounts and complex smart-contract ecosystems substantially hinder the tracing of illicit cryptocurrency fund flows. Existing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have achieved promising performance in blockchain fraud detection, yet their static node- or edge-level predictions do not naturally generalize to multi-hop fund tracing. Meanwhile, existing tracing methods mainly rely on predefined heuristics to capture multi-hop relationships, limiting their adaptive reasoning capabilities. To bridge this gap, we introduce CryptoFlowBench, a benchmark constructed from authoritative reports on cryptocurrency-related illicit incidents, with four tasks spanning local to multi-hop fund tracing. These tasks pose substantial challenges to existing learning- and heuristic-based methods, particularly in complex multi-hop scenarios. We therefore propose ChainSleuth, a graph-tool-augmented agent that iteratively reasons, invokes graph tools, and updates its tracing trajectory, enabling adaptive information acquisition and recovery from erroneous paths. Experiments show that no baseline consistently dominates all four tasks, revealing substantial gaps between local fraud detection and multi-hop fund tracing. ChainSleuth achieves notable improvements on multi-hop tasks, demonstrating the potential of agentic graph reasoning for cryptocurrency fund investigation.

title: EgoAlign: Situated 3D Understanding without Situation Descriptions
abstract: Situated 3D Question Answering requires models to interpret a 3D scene relative to an agent's pose. Existing methods commonly convey that pose through a natural-language situation description, which may be unavailable or costly to obtain in real-world deployments. While some methods additionally incorporate numerical pose, we find that randomly shuffling the agent pose causes little performance degradation, indicating limited functional dependence on the numerical pose. To address this gap, we introduce EgoAlign, a simple 3D language model that represents a scene in an agent-centric coordinate frame, together with a dedicated egocentric alignment stage comprising four complementary tasks: object category recognition, egocentric direction prediction, metric distance estimation, and spatial relation prediction. This stage teaches the model to consistently interpret scene geometry relative to the agent's pose before task-specific fine-tuning. EgoAlign achieves the strongest performance on SQA3D, Real-3DQA, and MSQA among compared methods while remaining highly efficient. More importantly, removing textual situation descriptions yields comparable or better downstream performance, whereas shuffling EgoAlign's numerical pose causes substantial degradation. These results show that EgoAlign establishes agent-centric spatial context directly from numerical pose without requiring textual situation descriptions.

title: A constrained log-HLS inequality and its associated Wasserstein flow
abstract: We study a log-Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev (log-HLS) inequality under constraints and a naturally induced Wasserstein flow. The constrained log-HLS inequality is dual, in a variational sense, to the constrained Trudinger-Moser-Onofri-Aubin inequality. The corresponding gradient-flow formulation leads to a parabolic-elliptic Patlak-Keller-Segel (PKS) system whose global dynamics exhibit a dichotomy between global existence and finite-time blow-up depending on the initial mass. Remarkably, the constraint raises the critical mass threshold of the flow by a factor of two compared with the unconstrained setting. This provides a distinct mechanism for suppressing blow-up from those arising in related formulations of the PKS-system, where blow-up is mitigated through additional effects such as a forcing term, coupling with a fluid equation, or the ambient flow generated by harmonic perturbations of the Newtonian potential.

title: An Analytical Study of ML Models for Behavioral Analytics in Catching Suspicious Payroll Activity
abstract: Machine learning methods are essential for enhancing behavioural analytics, enabling automatic pattern discovery and adaptive learning.Supervised learning models benefit from detecting known instances of fraud when labeled data are available.In contrast, unsupervised and semi-supervised methods can detect previously unknown anomalies without clearly defined labels indicating whether the data are fraudulent.Furthermore, deep learning models, including autoencoders and recurrent neural networks, can learn complex, nonlinear, and temporal dependencies in payroll data.All these features enable machine learning-based systems to keep up with changes in payroll practices, the workforce, and fraud strategies, thereby enhancing detection accuracy and resilience.In practice, data imbalance, feature selection, model interpretability, scalability, and concept drift have a significant impact [7].Various machine learning models have different strengths and weaknesses based on the features of payroll data and operational limitations [8] [9].Consequently, an analytical study should be conducted systematically to determine the effectiveness of ML models in behavioural analytics for detecting suspicious payroll activity. A. Structure of the PaperThis paper is organized as follows: Section II payroll activity and suspicious activity analysis.Section III Behavioral analytic framework for payroll monitoring Section IV.Machine learning model for behavioral analysis.The literature review is presented in Section V, and the conclusions and prospective research are discussed in Section VI.

title: A Hybrid Agentic RAG Architecture with Knowledge Graphs and Text-to-SQL for Automating Citizen Services in a Public Scientific Institution
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can produce plausible but incorrect content, a risk that is unacceptable when public institutions disclose scientific and legal information. This study presents and evaluates a hybrid agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system that automates first-level responses to citizen information requests at the Marine Institute of Peru (IMARPE). A baseline analysis of 196 requests showed a mean response time of 12 business days, above the 10-day legal limit, and identified 26.9% of them as routine, data-extractable queries. The system, developed under CRISP-DM, uses LangGraph to route each query to a LightRAG knowledge graph (Neo4j) built from institutional yearbooks, to a Text-to-SQL agent that queries the IMARSIS relational database through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), or to both, with Gemini 2.5 Flash as the foundation model and a referral protocol for out-of-scope requests. Five institutional domain experts rated 30 test cases, with mean scores of 4.45/5 for factual accuracy, 4.10/5 for completeness, and 4.57/5 for clarity. Mean end-to-end software latency was 20.43 s (maximum 49.20 s), and 30 pilot users rated usability at 80.42 on the System Usability Scale (Cronbach’s α = 0.96). These preliminary, single-site results indicate that combining graph-based and SQL-based grounding is feasible for routine citizen-information services; comparison with simpler baselines remains pending.

title: Can Large Language Models Identify Technical Terms in Documents Like Human Annotators?
abstract: Processing technical terms in documents is essential for digital libraries and knowledge organisation, supporting applications such as scholarly search, information retrieval, and domain terminology construction. While document-level term identification, a sub-task of automatic term extraction (ATE), has been tackled as a sequence labelling task, the emergence of large language models (LLMs) opens new avenues for prompt-based extraction. However, evaluation practices have persistently relied on simple success or failure against a single gold standard, without analysing how model behaviours align with human annotations, especially on borderline cases where annotators disagree. To address this issue, this study investigates to what extent LLMs can perform term identification using prompt instructions mirroring human annotator conditions. By evaluating multiple commercial and open-weight LLMs against double human annotations in ACL RD-TEC 2.0, an ATE benchmark, we show that LLMs achieve performance close to human annotators (up to 76.6% F1, within 5 percentage points of the inter-human agreement of 81.6%), with open-weight 30B-scale models outperforming larger commercial counterparts. Crucially, our analysis reveals a distinctly conservative nature: LLMs reliably extract terms on which humans consistently agree, but omit terms on which humans disagree. Our findings reveal the limitations of relying on a single gold standard, highlighting the need for annotator-aligned prompting and controllable precision–recall tuning.

title: Tikhonov-Stabilized Bezier Representation Forecasting for Training-free Diffusion Acceleration
abstract: Diffusion models, particularly Diffusion Transformers, achieve strong image and video generation quality but remain expensive at inference time due to repeated denoiser evaluations. Feature caching offers a deployment-friendly acceleration strategy by reusing or predicting intermediate representations without retraining the generator or modifying the sampler. However, existing cache-then-forecast methods often rely on Taylor-style finite-difference extrapolation, which can become unstable over longer cache intervals, and typically predict local module outputs whose errors may accumulate through subsequent denoiser blocks. We propose \textbf{BeziCast}, a training-free diffusion acceleration framework that forecasts output-proximal denoising representations using low-order B'ezier trajectories. BeziCast estimates B'ezier control points via Tikhonov-stabilized fitting, providing a smooth, capacity-controlled temporal parameterization that avoids explicit high-order derivative estimation and decouples trajectory capacity from cache-query density. To moderate aggressive extrapolation, we further derive equivalent forecasting weights and introduce a convex-hull-inspired guardrail that detects high-risk predictions and softly pulls them toward a conservative simplex-projected estimate. Extensive evaluations across advanced image and video diffusion models demonstrate the effectiveness of BeziCast. In particular, BeziCast accelerates FLUX.1 by up to (4.79\times) and HunyuanVideo by up to (4.11\times), while preserving substantially better generation quality than competing acceleration baselines.

title: The isoperimetric problem for four-dimensional parallelohedra
abstract: The honeycomb and Kelvin problems ask how space can be partitioned into cells of equal volume with the least surface area. We resolve this question in four dimensions for convex bodies that tile space by translations, showing that the regular 24-cell uniquely minimizes surface area at fixed volume. We develop a framework combining an exact deficit identity, valid in every dimension, with a descent argument. As a consequence, the regular 24-cell also minimizes surface area among such tiles containing a fixed ball.

title: Improving LLM Reliability Through Adaptive Detection
abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) transition from isolated research prototypes into integrated production systems, they encounter a critical safety-utility trade-off. Conventional safety mechanisms typically force a binary operational choice: either deploy strict, static guardrails that prevent harmful outputs but induce severe over-refusal of benign queries, or utilize relaxed controls that preserve usability at the cost of exposing users to unsafe generation. Furthermore, approaches that rely on scalar confidence signals lack contextual awareness, and monolithic API guardrails often introduce prohibitive latency bottlenecks. To resolve this socio-technical dilemma, we propose a multi-dimensional Adaptive Abstention System that models LLM refusal as a context-sensitive, dynamic decision-making process. Grounded in a Lagrangian risk minimization framework, our architecture automatically calibrates its abstention thresholds in real-time based on domain sensitivity and historical user trust. The system evaluates prompt risk across five orthogonal dimensions: safety, predictive confidence, knowledge boundaries, contextual appropriateness, and conversational repetition. To ensure low-latency inference, these detectors are arranged in a 4-level cost-sensitive cascade. Detector weights were optimized via Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization, shifting reliance from raw perplexity to distribution entropy and epistemic hedging. Extensive empirical evaluation across 10,000+ benchmark interactions (including AdvBench, ToxiGen, and XSTest) demonstrates that the proposed architecture achieves a Macro-F1 of 0.957 while reducing benign false-positive refusals by up to 80\% in specialized domains. Operational stress testing confirms production viability, successfully sustaining 895 requests per second with a 99th-percentile (P99) latency of 110 ms and an expected fast-path execution time of 4.3 ms on consumer-grade hardware.

title: The Model Is in the Wrong Seat
abstract: Agents today start from one premise: take the person in the control seat and put a model there instead. That seat was shaped around a person, and a model doesn't fit it. The fix isn't a better model or a better harness. It's a different starting point. This essay introduces AI-Oriented Programming and its two principles: assume the model can be wrong at any time without telling you, and assume the system will live in a world of agents. Chapter 0 of the AI-Oriented Programming series, first published on LinkedIn and X on October 12, 2026.

title: An Improved Retrieval-Augmented Generation Agent for UAV Situation Awareness Report Generation
abstract: Accurate and timely UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) situation awareness is essential for early warning and operational decision-making in low-altitude security, yet the manual analysis of large-scale heterogeneous data is resource-intensive and introduces delays. This study proposes IRAG-UAVSA (Improved Retrieval-Augmented Generation—Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Situation Awareness) Agent, an autonomous situation-awareness report-generation framework based on an improved retrieval-augmented generation architecture. The framework integrates real-time UAV descriptors, including platform type, intent, and threat level, with four task-specific hierarchical knowledge bases. A dual-loop pipeline combines evidence-template-guided hybrid retrieval and cross-encoder reranking with high-level LLM (Large Language Model) reflection, structured evidence filling, rule-based validation, and threshold-triggered iterative retry. A three-level evaluation framework was designed, comprising process-level RAG metrics, automatic natural language evaluation, and human–LLM collaborative scoring. Across 49 domain-screened test inputs, IRAG-UAVSA Agent achieved 93.0% knowledge coverage, 4.1% hallucination, and 91.7% logical consistency, while also obtaining the best SummaC (0.67) and VeriScore (0.83) results among the evaluated baselines. The results indicate that iterative retrieval with explicit evidence constraints can substantially improve the factual grounding, traceability, and practical utility of LLM-generated UAV situation-awareness reports.

title: Fourteen reusable building blocks (RBBs) for representing decision-making in agent-based models: a compilation on AGENTBLOCKS providing practical guidance and ways forward
abstract: Agent-based models (ABMs) are widely used to study socio–environmental systems. By integrating environmental modelling with behavioural theories, they enable to analyse how decision-making processes shape environmental outcomes. To speed up model development and enable cumulative theorising, it has been proposed to modularise components relevant across applications as reusable building blocks (RBBs). This paper describes an example of adopting the idea in practice using AGENTBLOCKS, a new open access platform for publishing RBBs. We present the first coordinated interdisciplinary effort of eleven modelling groups to identify, extract, review, and publish 14 decision-making RBBs from existing ABMs using AGENTBLOCKS. From this compilation, we extracted a decision tree to identify and scope reusable model components. Using a mixed-methods approach combining RBB criteria assessment, thematic coding of editorial feedback, and contributor surveys, we suggest empirically informed practices and next steps to lower the barrier for reusable coding practices in socio–environmental applications.

title: Global advances in Generative AI for renewable energy and implications for sustainable energy transitions in Africa
abstract: Abstract Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is being investigated for renewable-energy forecasting, optimisation, predictive maintenance, synthetic-data generation, and infrastructure planning. This study reviews global advances and critically assesses their implications for Africa's sustainable energy transition. It aims to: (i) map GenAI applications in renewable-energy systems; (ii) distinguish demonstrated results from proposed African opportunities; (iii) evaluate evidence quality, transferability, and deployment feasibility; and (iv) identify context-specific research and policy priorities. A systematic review was reported using PRISMA 2020, with the PRALSMA AI-assisted workflow used to support, but not replace, researcher-led screening and synthesis. OpenAlex records published from 2020 to May 2026 were screened, yielding 75 included studies. Manual analysis was triangulated with ChatGPT Project and NotebookLM, and findings were weighted by methodological quality, evidence maturity, and relevance to African data, grid, infrastructure, institutional, and cost conditions. The corpus remains geographically imbalanced: five of the 75 included studies report an African institutional affiliation (Morocco, Nigeria, and South Africa, with further co-affiliations in Tunisia and Gabon), and most quantitative outcomes still derive from non-African simulations, prototypes, or case studies. Consequently, reported error, cost, emission, and accuracy improvements are treated as source-specific rather than directly transferable African effects. Near-term priorities are controlled pilots of lightweight, explainable, offline-capable decision support and synthetic-data methods; compute-intensive diffusion, agentic, digital-twin, and imitation-learning applications require further validation. GenAI may support African renewable-energy transitions, but benefits depend on local datasets, reliable fallback procedures, lifecycle environmental assessment, workforce capacity, governance, and staged field validation.

title: Scaling Inference-Time Compute with Teams of Coding Agents
abstract: Multi-agent systems promise a new axis for scaling inference: rather than having one agent think longer or sample more attempts, a task is split across many agents that work in parallel and coordinate. However, in practice, more agents can easily produce duplicate work, coordination failures, and higher costs. We therefore formulate team design as a compute allocation problem: starting from a solo agent, where should additional inference compute go to reach the reward-cost Pareto frontier? We build a minimal multi-agent harness from the ground up and trace this frontier by varying, one at a time, the workflow stage at which a lead delegates to its workers (planning, implementation, or verification), the models that form the team, and the number of workers. On ProgramBench, teams outperform solo agents but cost three to seven times as much. With the right compute allocation, however, a heterogeneous 17-agent team comes within 1.4 points of a strong homogeneous 5-agent team at 70% lower cost. This efficiency stems from three findings. First, planning is the most valuable use of workers: in a homogeneous team whose lead decides how many workers to spawn, a lead that delegates only planning to its workers, and then implements and verifies the code itself, matches the reward of a lead that delegates to workers throughout planning, implementation, and verification, at half the cost. Second, cheap models pay off as planners but not as implementers: a strong lead with cheap planners recovers 47.5% of the reward gain of an all-strong team for only 13.9% of its additional cost, whereas cheap implementers lower reward. Third, planners keep improving reward as the team grows, whereas implementers and verifiers plateau beyond four workers. Together, our results offer a guide to spending an agent budget where it counts, given the task, cost, and latency constraints a user has.

title: Ghost unitaries for loss-resilient photonic resource-state generation
abstract: Entangled few-photon states, such as Bell and Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) states, are central resources for discrete-variable photonic quantum information processing. In many architectures, these states are generated probabilistically by first heralding single photons from biphoton sources and then interfering them in linear-optical circuits. In this work, we show that the entanglement structure of said biphoton sources can be directly exploited for noise-engineering to deliver higher quality resource states. Using the transpose identity of multi-mode squeezed vacuum states, we introduce "ghost-unitary" implementations in which the target resource-generation interferometer is applied to the heralding modes rather than to the delivered resource modes. When the dominant imperfection is interferometric loss, this relocation converts direct amplitude damping of the output into false-positive heralding events that require both higher-pair emission and photon loss. In the low-squeezing regime, these events are parametrically suppressed, yielding higher-fidelity conditional resource states. We analyze this mechanism for single-qubit states, two-photon NOON states, Bell states, and a family of $n$-qubit GHZ states, as well as for single-qubit teleportation and type-I-fusion-based resource growth. Across these examples, we delineate finite parameter regimes in which ghost-unitary implementations outperform direct implementations, with particular relevance to frequency-bin photonics where active linear-optical transformations can be relatively lossy. We also prove that, in the setting considered here, the direct implementation of the $n$-GHZ family delivers identically damped outputs: equivalent to the ideal state followed by uniform amplitude damping. This extends the known $n=2,3$ cases and provides a structural result of independent interest for photonic quantum information processing.

title: DexNinja: Learning Robust Dexterous Cutting Policy with a Real-to-Sim-to-Real Data Engine
abstract: Cutting a piece of food looks effortless in human hands. For a robot, however, every cut is a high-contact interaction with a deformable, elasto-plastic object whose behavior changes with pose, contact mode, and cutting stage. Collecting real-world data is expensive and wasteful: each trial typically contaminates or damages the food, so obtaining scalable real world data for dexterous cutting is expensive and difficult. Simulation is an appealing alternative, but a large sim-to-real gap exists in both physics and perception. This gap is especially severe for topology-changing interactions like cutting, where small errors in contact, friction, or material and elasticity responses quickly compound. We propose \textsc{DexNinja}, a real2sim2real framework that turns a handful of real demonstrations into a dense and realistic training distribution. \textsc{DexNinja} (i) reconstructs object instances from real captures, (ii) randomizes physically meaningful parameters under category-level constraints, and (iii) produces augmented dexterous manipulation episodes using a custom differentiable simulator that couples robot dynamics, tactile contact, and deformable cutting. We evaluate \textsc{DexNinja} on a dexterous food-slicing task and show that (1) with tens of real demonstrations and hundreds of augmented simulator data, the success rate could reach more than 60\%. (2) the augmented data consistently improves success rates when only using real data with more than 20\% via sim-to-real, and (3) the resulting policies generalize to out-of-distribution objects with varying shapes and sizes.

title: DDVR-Net: Degradation-Aware Decoupling and Visibility-Guided Restoration for Historical Document Recognition
abstract: Historical document analysis is crucial for cultural heritage preservation and low-resource language digitization. However, real historical documents often suffer from severe degradation, such as ink erosion and structural damage, causing mixed-visibility character sequences. Conventional OCR systems struggle in such evidence-limited scenarios, while contextual language models may over-correct visually clear characters. To address these challenges, we propose DDVR-Net, a degradation-aware decoupling and visibility-guided restoration framework for historical document recognition. DDVR-Net decouples intrinsic glyph structures from physical corruption at the feature level and predicts local visibility to estimate character reliability. A contextual decoder is selectively activated through a visibility-guided gate, restoring degraded characters while preserving clear visual recognition. Furthermore, we construct a low-resource multilingual benchmark covering Tibetan, Mongolian, and Uyghur scripts with 187000 document pairs, combining large-scale synthetic data and progressive training with real-world annotations to reduce the synthetic-to-real gap. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DDVR-Net consistently outperforms existing methods across three languages and diverse reading orders, providing an effective framework and benchmark for low-resource historical document recognition. Code and Benchmark: https://github.com/Shajiu/DDVR-Net

title: Explaining Heterogeneous Treatment Effects with Causal Forests and the Hoeffding Functional Decomposition
abstract: The estimation of heterogeneous treatment effects is a central objective of causal inference. However, state-of-the-art algorithms to solve this task are based on machine learning principles, and thus behave as black boxes. Consequently, the identification of covariates driving heterogeneity remains a challenging and open problem. To address this limitation, we introduce CausalTreeHFD, an interpretable extension of causal forests, based on the Hoeffding functional decomposition adapted to tree ensembles. Our approach decomposes predictions of conditional average treatment effects (CATE) into contributions from individual covariates and pairwise interactions, providing a direct characterization of the factors driving treatment effect heterogeneity. We establish the consistency of CausalTreeHFD, which converges towards the Hoeffding decomposition of the underlying CATE function, under standard assumptions for the analysis of causal forests. Experiments on simulated and real datasets show that CausalTreeHFD accurately identifies relevant covariates and interactions, and precisely recovers their contributions to heterogeneous treatment effects.

title: Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare: Methods, Benefits, and Challenges for Trustworthy Clinical Decision Support
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly studied for tasks such as medical-image analysis, risk prediction, and clinical decision support. However, strong predictive performance does not by itself show why a model reached a particular conclusion or whether that conclusion is appropriate for a patient. This paper reviews explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods that can make healthcare predictions more understandable to clinicians and other stakeholders. A focused narrative review was conducted using foundational work on local explanations and Shapley-value-based feature attribution, a healthcare-focused review, and World Health Organization guidance on AI ethics. The paper compares model-specific and model-agnostic explanations, with particular attention to LIME, SHAP, and visual explanation methods. The review indicates that explanations can support error analysis, communication, and model auditing, but they should not be treated as proof that a prediction is correct, fair, or clinically safe. Explanation quality depends on data quality, model behaviour, the intended user, and the clinical context. The paper proposes a practical evaluation framework combining predictive performance, explanation fidelity, stability, clinical usefulness, fairness checks, and human oversight. It concludes that XAI should be integrated into the full lifecycle of clinical AI systems rather than added only after model development. Index Terms—Explainable AI, healthcare, clinical decision support, interpretability, SHAP, LIME.

title: AI for Solar Energy Systems
abstract: The rapid expansion of solar energy has accelerated the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to improve forecasting accuracy, photovoltaic performance, intelligent control, fault diagnosis, energy storage management, and smart grid operation. Recent advances in machine learning, deep learning, Digital Twins, Physics-Informed Machine Learning, Edge AI, Federated Learning, and Generative AI have transformed solar energy systems into more adaptive and data-driven infrastructures. Despite these advances, challenges related to data quality, model generalization, computational efficiency, cybersecurity, and explainability continue to limit large-scale deployment. An integrated perspective is presented by connecting AI applications across photovoltaic systems, solar thermal technologies, energy storage, and intelligent energy networks within a unified renewable energy ecosystem. Emerging research trends and future directions highlight the evolution toward AI-native energy systems that support efficient, resilient, and sustainable intelligent societies.

title: Structure-Preserving Reinforcement Learning for Language Models: Leveraging Geometry
abstract: We propose a geometric framework for structure-preserving reinforcement learning in the fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs), grounded in Lie algebraic geometry. The approach systematically identifies geometric constraints in representation spaces by analyzing semantic transformations and detecting cases where embed- dings exhibit approximate Lie group structures. When such structure is present, we introduce reinforcement learning algorithms that respect these constraints through projection-based policy gradient updates. We provide theoretical guarantees of convergence and derive sample complexity bounds that depend on the intrinsic geomet- ric dimensionality rather than the full parameter space. The framework is particularly effective when language representations reveal coherent geometric patterns that encode semantic relations. Although empirical validation remains ongoing, this work establishes a principled foundation for integrating geometric priors into language model alignment, offering improved efficiency, stability, and interpretability from the perspectives of differential geometry and representation theory.

title: Strong Solvers, Leaky Tutors: Evaluating Answer Leakage in LLM Math Tutors
abstract: Educational digital libraries may grant large language model (LLM) tutors access to worked solutions, but access to repository content should not automatically authorize a model to reveal final answers. This study evaluates whether LLM tutors can leverage private solution context to generate pedagogical hints without disclosing final answers to students. Four models, two general instruction-following models and two math-specialized models, are evaluated across 5,000 aligned problem–message cases per condition, constructed from 500 MATH benchmark problems paired with ten fixed student prompts that ask for, or attempt to confirm, the final answer. Three prompting strategies are compared: a plain assistant prompt, a basic tutoring prompt, and a two-step method that generates a private solution before producing numbered hints. The basic tutoring prompt reduces detected answer leakage from 47.4% to 0.3% for GPT-4o-mini and from 30.2% to 1.0% for LLaMA-3.1, but produces no comparable improvement for Qwen2.5-Math or DeepSeek-Math. Under identical strict hint rules, adding private solution context has minimal effect on GPT but significantly improves tutoring compliance for LLaMA; Qwen produces the most accurate private solutions yet shows the highest leakage and solution-to-hint overlap. These results indicate that private solution access can support hint generation in some architectures but is not a reliable answer-withholding mechanism on its own. For educational digital libraries, access to solution content and authorization to disclose it should be treated as distinct access-control decisions.

title: Assessing the Performance of AI Models in Misinformation Detection Using Predefined Social Noise Constructs
abstract: Social media platforms generate vast volumes of user-generated content that often obscure meaningful discourse, a phenomenon conceptualized as social noise. While existing misinformation detection methods primarily focus on factual verification, they largely overlook the role of social noise in amplifying misinformation. This study assesses the performance of six text-based models and a graph neural network (GNN) in mitigating the effects of misinformation using predefined social noise constructs. The dataset consists of 500,000 tweets collected from the X platform using the Ukraine hashtag during the Russia-Ukraine conflict from March 2024 to March 2025. Advanced machine learning models achieve strong performance, with accuracies ranging from 79.94% to 97.17%. RoBERTa demonstrates the highest performance, with an accuracy of 97.17%, Cohen's kappa of 0.9660, MCC of 0.9660, and AUC of 0.9977. The GNN achieves an accuracy of 64.52% and an AUC of 0.899, demonstrating performance above random-chance classification by exploiting the relational structure between tweets. All text-based models achieve kappa values greater than 0.75, indicating substantial overall agreement. Explainable AI analysis using LIME reveals that 89.6% of predictive weight is attributed to contextual features rather than isolated keywords. The findings highlight that integrating social noise into AI pipelines enhances misinformation detection and supports more effective mitigation strategies in large-scale social media environments.

title: AutoMARS: Automatic and Scalable Multi-Agent Large Language Model Framework for Supply Chain Risk Assessment
abstract: We propose AutoMARS (Automatic Multi-Agent Risk Assessment), an agentic framework for automatic and scalable comparative risk assessment in supply chain networks. The framework enables end-to-end execution of analytical workflows by automatically planning tasks, coordinating specialized agents, invoking external analytical tools, and synthesizing domain-specific results into integrated risk evaluations. AutoMARS further supports scalable risk comparison across multiple locations by parallelizing independent analytical tasks. The framework adopts a multi-domain, multi-agent, and multi-tool architecture that integrates heterogeneous risk factors from socioeconomic, disaster, environmental, and transportation domains. Through coordinated agent interactions and tool integration, AutoMARS enables structured, systematic, and interpretable comparative analysis to support supply chain risk-aware location evaluation.

title: Spectral Costs of Multinomial and Residual Resampling in High-Dimensional Particle Ensembles: A Free-Probability Analysis
abstract: Resampling is the standard remedy against weight degeneracy in particle filters, yet its effect on the spectrum of the particle second-moment matrix is poorly understood. We study a single resampling step for a d-dimensional ensemble of N particles with d/N -> c. For any unbiased scheme, the resampled empirical second-moment matrix dominates its pre-resampling counterpart in conditional convex order, while the conditional mean is preserved; the excess second spectral moment equals the Frobenius energy of the resampling perturbation. For multinomial resampling, the empirical count law converges to the mixed-Poisson law determined by the limiting weight law. For residual resampling, the count law is determined by the joint limit of floor-fraction pairs: we classify all residual limits of weight sequences converging to delta_1 in law as a one-parameter family between the deterministic identity and the full multinomial count law. Each count law feeds a common covariance-side spectral map, yielding exact consequences: a closed-form zero-eigenvalue mass, a rank-and-spectral-gap transition with a universal lower edge benchmark, computable regular edges, unbounded right support, and scheme-specific second-moment costs. The effective sample size determines one bulk statistic but cannot determine the limiting spectrum. Pre-registered numerical experiments confirm the theory at every level.

title: Pixels or Code? Benchmarking Instruction-Guided Visual Artifact Operation
abstract: Visual artifacts such as charts, technical diagrams, webpages, and document pages underpin scientific, commercial, and engineering workflows. Editing these artifacts requires direct modification, dependency-aware updates, preservation of unaffected content, and compliance with domain constraints. We define this capability as Visual Artifact Operation (VAO). Prior benchmarks test parts of this problem, including cascading updates in charts. We study direct edits, dependent updates, and preservation across visual domains and pixel, code, and agent paradigms under one image-only protocol. We introduce Visual Artifact Operation Bench (VAO-Bench), comprising 1,573 manually screened tasks across nine artifact categories and three difficulty levels. VAO-Bench uses executable artifacts and deterministic rendering to trace reference transformations and annotate direct edits, dependent updates, and preservation constraints. All systems receive the same source image and instruction; we evaluate pixel-space editors, code-generating multimodal systems, and tool-using agents on direct-edit accuracy, dependency-aware update, content preservation, domain validity, and visual quality. Experiments show that executable-code systems better support dependent updates, while pixel-space editors offer faster execution and strong visual quality. Explicitly stating dependencies improves both paradigms, identifying implicit-update inference as a central bottleneck. VAO-Bench provides a reproducible foundation for dependable visual artifact editing across generation paradigms.

title: Measuring LLM Refusal Rates: XSTest False Positives Under 5% or Skip
abstract: Gate LLM selection on XSTest false-positive rates under 5% or skip the model. Verify the live, complete option and compare like-for-like totals before committing. title: Get In, Decide, Prove: companion dataset (access census records, pilot capture hashes, rubric v0.1, and aggregates of the declared assessment of 330 merchants)
abstract: Companion dataset of "Get In, Decide, Prove: A Merchant-Side Readiness Benchmark for Agentic Commerce" (arXiv:2610.17378, https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.17378). It holds: the home-page access census of 555 merchant sites observed on 30 September 2026 under two declared agent profiles, with site identities removed; the capture records of the four pilot assessments of 29 September 2026 (merchants anonymised, capture hashes only); the rubric of the twenty readiness metrics, version 0.1; and the aggregate results of the declared assessment of 330 merchants observed on 3 and 7 October 2026, with the repeat of 8 October. No host name, URL, page text, merchant name or payment processor is included. Each file is described in the README.

title: Ontological Engineering and Semantic Topical Authority in Large Language Models: A Holistic Framework for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)
abstract: This paper presents an end-to-end ontological engineering framework based on the Holistic Semantic SEO and Topical Authority principles formalized by Koray Tuğberk Gübür, adapted specifically for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and neural search retrieval in frontier Large Language Models (LLMs). We define the topological requirements for closed-loop topical authority graphs that eliminate internal semantic cannibalization, enforce Entity-Attribute-Value (EAV) graph coherence, and maximize contextual retrieval probability in architectures such as Google Gemini, OpenAI GPT, Anthropic Claude, and Perplexity AI. Empirical validation across enterprise DFY services (POS1 SEO Agency) and vocational education platforms (Aprender21) demonstrates sustained organic commercial performance with $0 in paid advertising spend.

title: A Two-way Interactive Secure Communication Model for Electric Energy Metering Data
abstract: INTRODUCTION: As power market reforms deepen, traditional unidirectional protocols (e.g., IEC 102) fail to meet the secure, real-time, and bidirectional data exchange requirements of modern power grids, leaving systems vulnerable to eavesdropping and tampering.OBJECTIVES: To ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and reliability of power data transmission by overcoming the pattern leakage vulnerabilities of traditional encryption, while satisfying the strict real-time and high-frequency demands of large-scale power systems.METHODS: Two schemes are designed: a pure SM4 symmetric encryption scheme for high-frequency data, and an SM2-SM4 hybrid scheme for advanced authentication. To enhance security, a novel ECB-CBC hybrid encryption mode is introduced for SM4. RESULTS: The proposed ECB-CBC hybrid mode effectively eliminates plaintext redundancy. Its Shannon entropy stabilizes at ~7.99 bits/byte (nearly touching the 8.0 theoretical ideal, vastly improving upon standard ECB's ~3.5 bits/byte). It also achieves an optimal inter-block avalanche effect of ~64 bits per block. The SM2-SM4 hybrid scheme's encryption time is only 15%-20% higher than that of pure SM4. Across 1-16 thread tests, the throughput of both SM4-based schemes grows linearly, outperforming RSA and fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) by several orders of magnitude.CONCLUSION: The proposed ECB-CBC hybrid architecture overcomes standard mode vulnerabilities and achieves the macro-level Strict Avalanche Criterion (SAC), significantly enhancing resistance to network attacks. Compared to traditional asymmetric and homomorphic encryption, the SM4 and SM2-SM4 schemes strike an optimal balance between robust security and computational efficiency for high-concurrency power system applications.

title: Fibonacci–Lucas Recurrence-Indexed Quaternionic Unitaries: Channel Convergence, Clifford Proximity, and Controlled Entanglement
abstract: We investigate the normalized operator geometry of the mixed Fibonacci–Lucas quaternion Qn = Fn + Lni + Fn+1j + Ln+1k. Standard quaternion representations associate this sequence with single-qubit unitary channels. We first establish a convergence theorem for quaternion sequences with two distinct real characteristic roots and a strictly dominant positive root. It gives an exact average gate infidelity to the limit and sharp projective-step asymptotics, including the degenerate constant-channel case. For the Fibonacci–Lucas assignment, orthogonal Binet coefficient vectors yield exact finite-index formulas with projective steps of order φ−2n and average gate infidelities of order φ−4n. Strict comparison of the five projective Clifford rotation classes proves that the limiting unitary has a unique nearest projective Clifford, the cyclic Pauli-axis permutation, with average gate fidelity 115+5/90≈0.884408. For the controlled family, product-input maximization gives concurrence 1−an2, while independent Haar averaging gives linear-entropy entangling power 21−an2/9. Both admit explicit algebraic limits. Reproducible matrix and high-precision scalar calculations verify these results. The analysis supplies exact convergence, finite-group, and entanglement benchmarks for a recurrence-indexed family without assuming Hamiltonian dynamics.

title: Can LLMs Reason Over Where and When? Benchmarking Spatiotemporal Synthesis in Crisis Response
abstract: Situational awareness during crises depends on synthesizing fragmented reports that vary across time, location, and source. Reliable crisis question answering must prioritize recent and nearby reports while reconciling updates that contradict earlier information. However, existing crisis datasets often provide insufficient evidence for systematically evaluating these capabilities. We audit evidence coverage across crisis-need queries and enrich under-covered cases with synthetic situational-awareness posts, constructing sequences of reports and updates that preserve spatiotemporal consistency. Using the enriched benchmark, we compare direct prompting, structured prompting, and ST-CrisisSynth, which applies query-dependent semantic, spatial, and temporal weights to re-rank evidence before generation. Human evaluation shows that ST-CrisisSynth achieves the highest correct-response rate (70.0%), improving by 3.3 percentage points over the strongest baseline. These findings suggest that selecting and organizing spatiotemporal evidence before generation supports more reliable crisis information synthesis.
