title: The Decomposition Dilemma: When Do Multi-Agent LLM Workflows Help Grounded Knowledge Generation?
abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) workflows increasingly decompose knowledge-intensive generation into planning, role assignment, subtask execution, and synthesis. Although this structure may support specialization, it also adds coordination and computational overhead. We present a preliminary task-level comparison of a Direct Generation Workflow and a Decomposed Generation Workflow under matched inputs and evaluation conditions. The study covers three grounded knowledge-generation tasks: public-event narrative synthesis, project-grounded research ideation, and scientific related-work generation. Across the evaluated configurations, decomposition produces the largest mean Task Quality Score (TQS) gain for research ideation (+0.053), a smaller gain for related-work generation (+0.025), and only a modest gain for public-event narrative synthesis (+0.013). These improvements require 95.1–126.2 seconds of additional runtime on average. The results provide preliminary evidence that the value of multi-agent decomposition is task-dependent.

title: ChemExplain: A Multimodal Benchmark for Explanatory Chemical Reasoning
abstract: Current chemistry benchmarks primarily evaluate outcome prediction or reaction pathway generation, but rarely test whether a model can explain why an observed chemical effect occurs. We introduce ChemExplain, a benchmark of 1,180 multiple-choice chemistry questions drawn from 383 peer-reviewed papers. Each question pairs a molecular or reaction image with an observed chemical effect and four candidate explanations, each associated with a different structural feature visible in the image. Answering requires the model to perceive the depicted structure, apply chemical knowledge, and identify which feature most directly explains the effect, a capability we term explanatory attribution. The correct feature-mechanism relation is derived from supporting evidence in the source paper rather than invented by the question-generation LLM. We construct the benchmark automatically with a multi-agent framework that applies progressive quality control at three stages and validate it with eight chemistry domain experts. The strongest evaluated model reaches 78.6% accuracy, leaving considerable room for improvement. On a 600-question expert-reviewed subset, reasoning-trace analysis classifies 71.4% of the strongest model's errors as attribution failures. Attribution is also the largest error category for the open-source and chemistry-specific models included in our analysis.

title: Photon-stimulated decay of $χ$-matched ancillas causes unheralded bit flips in bosonic codes
abstract: Bosonic codes often read out their syndrome with a transmon ancilla whose computational levels $g$ and $f$ have equal parity and matched dispersive shifts: a decay $f\to e$ is then heralded and leaves the code intact, while the direct $f\to g$ is forbidden by parity. We show that the photons of the code open this decay at first order in the ancilla's decay rate. Dressing by the code mode lets the charge noise that limits the ancilla's $T_1$ drive a photon-stimulated Raman decay $|f,n\rangle\to|g,n+1\rangle$, at $(n+1)(χ_{ge}/2g_{01})^2$ times the $f\to e$ rate for a smooth noise spectrum. When the matching is set by the detuning, the decay costs $\approxΓ_{fe}/α$ per gate and photon, whatever the coupling strength; a deliberate mismatch or matching by a drive lowers this cost, and a qubit ancilla has no such channel. The opened decay is unheralded and flips a cat with probability $\approx 1/2$; being first order, it overtakes the second-order double decay $f\to e\to g$ as the ancilla improves. In a microscopic model of the Ocelot repetition cat code, it makes the bit-flip floor of the gates grow linearly with the cat size, by a factor 1.2-1.7 from four to ten photons, which would limit the noise bias to $\sim 10^3$. The published gate data end at four photons and do not yet test this growth.

title: Time Window Optimization for Motor Imagery Classification via Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Online motor imagery-based brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) typically decode continuous EEG using fixed-length sliding windows that may be misaligned with neural events. Existing window optimization methods often evaluate windows independently, overlooking temporal dependencies and potentially producing fragmented or physiologically implausible selections. We propose Temporal Structure Embedded Reinforcement Learning (TSE-RL), a framework that incorporates prior knowledge of MI event structure into a constrained Markov decision process for adaptive window optimization. First, TSE-RL assigns each window an explicit semantic role through Discard, Onset, Sustain, or Offset actions, extending binary retain/discard decisions to event-level alignment. Second, a finite-state machine masks invalid actions to enforce the temporal order of MI phases and promote physiologically plausible window sequences. Third, a Transformer-based history encoder captures dependencies across windows, improving training stability and computational efficiency compared with recurrent architectures. TSE-RL is plug-and-play and can be integrated with diverse MI classifiers. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate consistent improvements in decoding performance in both cross-session and cross-subject settings. Visualization analyses further suggest that the learned window selection policy aligns with neurophysiological principles.

title: Chain Dimension Scaling: Communication-Efficient Loop-Style Scaling for Industrial Short-Video Ranking
abstract: Industrial recommendation rankers keep scaling in width and depth to billions of parameters, but this increasingly incurs costs in parameter growth, distributed communication overhead, and training inefficiency. We introduce \underline{C}hain \underline{D}imension \underline{S}caling (CDS), a scaling strategy orthogonal to width and depth. CDS repeatedly applies a single feature-interaction block with parameters shared across iterations, so the number of iterations (the chain length) becomes a new scaling dimension that adds no parameters. A lightweight intra-chain residual connection stabilizes optimization and improves quality. CDS enables two regimes. In the \emph{compression regime}, shallow blocks with a longer chain match deeper baselines with fewer parameters and faster training; in the \emph{quality-scaling regime}, increasing chain length under a fixed parameter budget yields consistent offline and online gains, suggesting the chain dimension adds modeling capacity beyond parameter reuse. We evaluate CDS in a large-scale multi-task short-video ranking system in production. In the compression regime, CDS stays within $0.03\%$ of baseline offline quality while reducing trainable parameters by 26.6\% and improving training throughput by 6.4\%, with neutral-to-positive online participation. In the quality-scaling regime, quality improves monotonically with chain length. Wall-clock analysis shows the efficiency gain comes mainly not from reduced FLOPs but from lower cross-device synchronization overhead and reduced optimizer update cost. These results position parameter-shared iterative computation as a practical, communication-efficient scaling axis for industrial ranking systems.

title: Pollard: Governed Semantic Execution Trees for Framework-Independent AI Agent Control and Replay
abstract: Agent frameworks can persist checkpoints, trace tool calls, and limit resource use, but these facilities often assign different identities to execution, governance, and replay. We present Pollard, a framework-independent runtime based on governed semantic execution trees. A step identity commits to canonical input, kind, attempt, and parent identity; the same tree records completion, refusal, resource settlement, and branch history. Strict replay returns a verified stored result without invoking the wrapped operation, while a transactional store coordinates reservations across concurrent workers. Under a signed deterministic freeze, two state-model replicas each executed the evaluation transitions without an invariant violation, retained-lease PostgreSQL groups were tested against exact limits, strict replay avoided external calls, and all semantic mutations were detected with no false alarms on the controls. A multi-pair framework matrix preserved reference behavior and verified the trees. A separate cost-capped hosted study exercised live provider paths, and every completed Pollard trial produced a verified tree. Together, the studies support the core mechanisms under explicit lease, boundary, and seal-custody assumptions.

title: MAIN DIRECTIONS AND RESULTS OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN THE FIELD OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
abstract: This scientific article highlights the main directions of scientific research in the field of artificial intelligence, the results achieved, and their significance in the development of modern society. It analyzes the developmental characteristics of areas such as machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, computer vision, robotics, and generative artificial intelligence. Opportunities arising from the application of artificial intelligence technologies in the fields of education, medicine, industry, economics, and information technology will also be considered.

title: What Users Value in Dance Learning Apps: Topic Modeling and Sentiment Analysis of App Store Reviews – Replication Data and Code
abstract: Replication data and code for the manuscript “What Users Value in Dance Learning Apps: Topic Modeling and Sentiment Analysis of App Store Reviews.” The package contains the de-identified review-level dataset (n = 2,469 Google Play reviews), the 500-review manual validation sample, the codebook, collection metadata, article tables, and a script that reproduces the reported results. Review texts are not included to protect reviewer privacy; they are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

title: Where and How We Talk to AI in Learning: A Scoping Review on the Placement and Communication Modalities of Pedagogical Conversational Agents in Higher EducationWhere and How We Talk to AI in Learning: A Scoping Review on the Placement and Communication Modalities of Pedagogical Conversational Agents in Higher Education
abstract: With the rapid advancements in artificial intelligence and large language models (LLMs), higher education institutions are increasingly integrating conversational interfaces to deliver personalised learning support, real-time scaffolding, and scalable feedback to students. Known as Pedagogical Conversational Agents (PCAs), these tools have evolved from simple rule-based chatbots into complex systems featuring diverse communication modalities (e.g., text, speech/voice, graphic/ visuals, and multimodal inputs) and varied digital placements (e.g., embedded Learning Management System (LMS), sidebars, floating overlays, and standalone web applications). While most of the literature evaluates the broad learning gains or technology acceptance of PCAs, limited research systematically examines how these agents are digitally situated in the user interface or how communication modalities shape pedagogical interactions. Following the JBI methodology for scoping reviews and PRISMA-ScR reporting standards, this review aims to map the current design and deployment landscape of PCAs in higher education. This review will synthesize the existing literature, illustrating how specific modality and placement configurations intersect across academic disciplines. Findings will provide evidence-based design guidelines for educational technologists, instructional designers, and researchers developing pedagogical conversational agents implemented into higher education.

title: DTKF: a sepsis early prediction framework based on large language model semantic augmentation and dual-teacher knowledge distillation
abstract: Sepsis is a life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection. Early and accurate prediction is crucial for reducing mortality. However, clinical settings often face challenges such as data scarcity, class imbalance, and the underutilization of unstructured clinical notes. Existing scoring systems and traditional machine learning models primarily rely on structured vital signs, failing to capture the rich semantic risk factors embedded in textual data. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in text understanding, their high computational costs and potential hallucinations hinder direct deployment in resource-constrained emergency settings. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel Dual-Teacher Knowledge Fusion (DTKF) framework. First, we introduce a semantic feature augmentation module that leverages DeepSeek to extract semantic risk probabilities from clinical notes and explicitly fuses them with structured vital signs to construct high-order hybrid features for the student model. Second, to prevent overfitting under small-sample conditions, we design a dual-source knowledge distillation strategy. This strategy integrates rule-based knowledge and data-driven semantic knowledge to construct hybrid teacher signals, regulating a lightweight logistic regression student model via soft-label supervision. Experiments on the MIMIC-IV dataset demonstrate that DTKF achieves an AUC of 0.796. This result not only achieves a higher AUC than traditional unimodal baselines but also improves performance by 6.6% compared to direct prediction using LLMs. This study effectively integrates rule-based and data-driven knowledge, enhances feature representation using textual information, and improves model performance and robustness through distillation techniques, providing a clinically valuable solution for sepsis early warning.

title: Applications of Generative AI for Advancing Scientific Content Production, Evaluation and Dissemination
abstract: Generative AI is becoming part of how scientific content is being produced, evaluated and communicated. Large language models (LLMs) can write science news, simulate readers, retrieve evidence, generate scientific hypotheses, write code, and execute research workflows. These capabilities create opportunities for accelerating scientific discovery and broadening access to scientific information, but they also introduce risks related to hallucination and trustworthiness. This doctoral dissertation studies how generative AI can support scientific content production and dissemination, while preserving trust, comprehension, and replicability. The completed work includes three components: (1) detecting LLM-generated science news through SANews and GFS, (2) evaluating science communication through reader learning using KnowledgeGain and LLMSim, and (3) benchmarking LLM agents for research replication with ReplicatorBench and ReplicatorAgent. The proposed work extends these directions toward learning-optimized science news generation, MESH for multimodal evidence-grounded hypothesis generation, and MERIT, a simulation-grounded framework for evaluating autonomous AI co-scientists and hypothesis testing in computational materials discovery. The overarching goal is to develop evaluation methods and AI systems that make scientific outputs not only fluent and scalable, but also grounded, useful, and interpretable.

title: BibNER-Werk: Bibliographic NER for Historical German Catalogs
abstract: General-purpose named entity recognition does not identify the title and responsible person needed to link historical German bibliographic catalog strings in the Deutsche Digitale Bibliothek (DDB) to GND Work authorities, since the task’s label set and centuries-spanning historical register have no counterpart in standard training corpora. This paper uses ISBD punctuation as a tiered silver labeling signal and evaluates a deterministic rule-based baseline alongside zero-shot, few-shot, and fine-tuned GLiNER-multi and fine-tuned XLM-R-large on a stratified, human-annotated gold set. The rule-based baseline beats both fine-tuned systems on untrained data; on trained data, only GLiNER-multi’s fine-tuning gains a real, confirmed precision advantage, and XLM-R-large’s never surpasses the rule.

title: Know-Thy-Not: Training-Free Targeted Negation in Dual-Encoder Vision-Language Models
abstract: Dual-encoder vision-language models systematically fail at negation, scoring ''a cat without a dog'' nearly identically to ''a cat with a dog.'' We show that this failure is inherent to the single-embedding framework. Under contrastive training, single-embedding methods can at best ignore the negated concept (dilution) but never penalize its presence (rejection). We propose Know-Thy-Not (KTN), a training-free method that introduces an image-side rejection dimension to penalize the negated concept directly in the visual representation. We also introduce COCO-Confusion, the first benchmark requiring genuine rejection to succeed. Across 9 backbones, KTN improves COCO-Confusion mAP by up to +25.6 over vanilla VLMs and +9.6 over the strongest existing method.

title: ModRes: A modification of the ResPlan dataset ready for floor plan analysis and graph machine learning
abstract: Floor plan datasets underpin computational analysis of building layouts, spatial connectivity and graph machine learning. However, publicly available datasets often require substantial preprocessing before they can be used reliably. We present ModRes, a cleaned and enriched version of the ResPlan dataset, containing 8,431 valid and unique residential floor plans. Invalid and duplicate floor plans are removed through a dedicated cleaning workflow, producing a ready-to-use dataset. For each floor plan, ModRes provides two-dimensional geometry, images, three-dimensional building representations and three complementary dual graphs in CSV and JSON formats with graph-, node- and edge-level features. Continuous and categorical graph attributes support machine learning workflows. We characterise the dataset using graph-based statistics and demonstrate its utility through a range of case studies. ModRes provides structured geometric, topological and semantic representations needed to automate spatial analysis and support machine learning-based workflows for building design and performance evaluation.

title: ML Engineering Agents - A Data Management Perspective
abstract: Machine learning engineering (MLE) agents are emerging as a new paradigm for automating end-to-end ML pipeline development. Using large language models for code generation and predictive performance as a machine-gradable feedback signal, these agents iteratively synthesize, execute, and refine pipeline code. Yet current systems are largely evaluated on pre-built, single-table benchmarks that abstract away key data management challenges. This tutorial introduces the foundations of MLE agents and highlights research opportunities for the database community. We cover how agents combine program synthesis with iterative and evolutionary optimization, and discuss open challenges in efficient pipeline execution, data discovery and augmentation over heterogeneous sources, reliability and debugging, as well as fairness and compliance. We connect these challenges to existing data management techniques and conclude with a hands-on session using contemporary MLE agents.

title: Learning Incompressible 3D Flows from Sparse Samples: A Set Transformer Approach to Divergence-Free Kernel Fitting
abstract: Recovering divergence-free velocity fields from sparse and corrupted observations requires reconciling physical consistency, expressive representations, and robustness to missing data. We introduce DFK-Former, a set-to-field transformer that reconstructs divergence-free velocity fields from sparse, noisy, and irregularly sampled 3D observations. The model is inherently invariant to the number and ordering of input samples and predicts the parameters of a divergence-free kernel representation, producing continuous, mesh-free velocity fields that satisfy incompressibility exactly by construction rather than approximately through soft constraints or projection operators. Unlike existing divergence-free kernel approaches, which estimate kernel coefficients via a separate optimization for each field, DFK-Former predicts these coefficients directly in a single forward pass. This eliminates costly iterative fitting while providing a learned prior that enables accurate reconstruction even when observations are insufficient to uniquely determine the field. To enhance representational power, we introduce adaptive and anisotropic divergence-free kernels that preserve exact incompressibility guarantees while capturing more complex flow structures. Extensive experiments across varying levels of sparsity, noise, and occlusion, including transfer to real Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) turbulence data, demonstrate substantial gains in both accuracy and efficiency. DFK-Former reduces endpoint error by up to 4.6x compared to per-field divergence-free-kernel optimization, while reconstructing each field in 7.5 ms instead of 9.8 s, yielding a speedup of more than three orders of magnitude. These results establish direct, feed-forward prediction of divergence-free kernel parameters as a practical and effective paradigm for physically consistent velocity-field reconstruction from sparse observations.

evidence.title: Learning Incompressible 3D Flows from Sparse Samples: A Set Transformer Approach to Divergence-Free Kernel Fitting
evidence.abstract: Recovering divergence-free velocity fields from sparse and corrupted observations requires reconciling physical consistency, expressive representations, and robustness to missing data. We introduce DFK-Former, a set-to-field transformer that reconstructs divergence-free velocity fields from sparse, noisy, and irregularly sampled 3D observations. The model is inherently invariant to the number and ordering of input samples and predicts the parameters of a divergence-free kernel representation, producing continuous, mesh-free velocity fields that satisfy incompressibility exactly by construction rather than approximately through soft constraints or projection operators. Unlike existing divergence-free kernel approaches, which estimate kernel coefficients via a separate optimization for each field, DFK-Former predicts these coefficients directly in a single forward pass. This eliminates costly iterative fitting while providing a learned prior that enables accurate reconstruction even when observations are insufficient to uniquely determine the field. To enhance representational power, we introduce adaptive and anisotropic divergence-free kernels that preserve exact incompressibility guarantees while capturing more complex flow structures. Extensive experiments across varying levels of sparsity, noise, and occlusion, including transfer to real Direct Numerical Simulation (DNS) turbulence data, demonstrate substantial gains in both accuracy and efficiency. DFK-Former reduces endpoint error by up to 4.6x compared to per-field divergence-free-kernel optimization, while reconstructing each field in 7.5 ms instead of 9.8 s, yielding a speedup of more than three orders of magnitude. These results establish direct, feed-forward prediction of divergence-free kernel parameters as a practical and effective paradigm for physically consistent velocity-field reconstruction from sparse observations.

title: SLS-Bench: A Benchmark for Incident Log Summarization with Synthetic Observability Data
abstract: As IT systems grow in complexity, automated agent-driven incident response becomes increasingly critical. A key capability for these agents is summarizing large log streams into human-readable reports. Further progress requires meaningfully evaluating this function, yet existing benchmarks leave end-to-end summarization from large log streams underexplored due to the prohibitive cost and complexity of collecting real-world data. We introduce SLS-Bench, a benchmark for incident log summarization featuring 90 tasks grounded in real-world incident reports, each with a synthetic log stream and a reference summary. To construct SLS-Bench, we developed a data generation pipeline that converts incident reports into structured incident models, which guide the generation of synthetic logs and reference summaries. This pipeline combines narrative grounding, explicit incident modeling, generator-verifier loops, and statistical comparisons with real-world log streams to produce realistic and controllable observability data. Our evaluation of 14 LLMs on SLS-Bench shows that while frontier models can produce useful summaries, they do so at substantial cost and latency, and open-weight models lag significantly. SLS-Bench provides a framework for systematic evaluation of log analysis agents and a scalable blueprint for future synthetic observability benchmarks.

title: Efeito de Dobra: nota técnica sobre a lista binária convencional e o peso de Hamming
abstract: Esta nota técnica apresenta o Efeito de Dobra (Folding Effect), uma construção formal sobre o conjunto das 32 palavras binárias de 5 bits. A partir de uma observação intuitiva — a dobra de uma fita de papel translúcida contendo uma lista binária — formaliza-se a operação de complementação antipodal J(x) = x ⊕ 11111 = 31 − x, demonstrando-se que o agrupamento recursivo em cinco etapas produz uma sequência decrescente de distâncias de Hamming entre representantes de blocos (5 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1) e a anulação da paridade XOR a partir da segunda etapa. A nota conclui que o Efeito de Dobra constitui uma construção algébrica rigorosa, autocontida e de escopo delimitado sobre a geometria do hipercubo booleano convencional.

title: OES-32 Dashboard: PyQt6 desktop view of a filtered synthetic 32-channel signal and its Welch PSD
abstract: OES-32 Dashboard is a self-contained PyQt6 + PyQtGraph desktop application that shows a rolling filtered waveform (channel 0) and a channel-averaged Welch power spectral density (0-50 Hz) for a simulated 32-channel signal. The GUI-free signal path (oes32_pipeline.py) applies a stateful 50 Hz IIR notch (Q = 30) and a 4th-order 0.5-45 Hz Butterworth bandpass at a nominal 250 Hz. The synthetic input is a 10 Hz test tone plus a 50 Hz mains-like tone in arbitrary units. Scope: synthetic stimuli only. It is not hardware, field, medical or certified control software, makes no physical, biological or clinical claim, and is not the normative OES-32 residual (see oes32-residual). Python 3.10+, PyQt6, PyQtGraph, NumPy and SciPy. pytest tests of the signal path and a headless start-up smoke test run in GitHub Actions. License: AGPL-3.0-only (commercial licence available).

title: A Privacy-Preserving Decentralized Partition-Autonomous Planning Method for Interconnected Multi-Microgrid Distribution Systems Driven by Federated Proximal Policy Optimization
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The rapid integration of distributed renewable energy and ICT infrastructure has made interconnected multi-microgrid distribution systems essential for low-carbon power grids, yet centralized coordination exposes sensitive operational data to privacy risks, including eavesdropping and membership inference attacks under 5G and edge computing environments.OBJECTIVES: This study resolves the tension between data privacy protection and decentralized collaborative planning by developing a unified federated reinforcement learning framework with formal privacy guarantees.METHODS: A privacy-preserving decentralized partition-autonomous planning method driven by federated proximal policy optimization is proposed. The network is divided into autonomous units, each performing local proximal policy optimization on local observations. A proximal term constrains update steps against Non-IID drift. A time-period adaptive differential privacy budget mechanism dynamically adjusts noise according to gradient sensitivity, complemented by a Shamir secret sharing-based secure aggregation protocol forming dual-layer protection.RESULTS: Experiments on the Baran-Wu 33-node test system show daily operational cost within 3.0% of the centralized benchmark, per round communication reduced by approximately 80% to 9.6 MB, voltage compliance at 98.4%, and membership inference attack AUC suppressed to 0.521DISCUSSION: The adaptive privacy budget reduces utility loss by 3.2 percentage points under strict privacy constraints versus fixed schemes, while secure aggregation maintains reliability under one PAU dropout with only 0.38% deviation. CONCLUSION: The proposed framework provides a feasible technical path for secure collaborative planning of large-scale interconnected multi-microgrid systems under practical ICT constraints.

title: High-Information-Density Knowledge Graph Retrieval Augmentation for Large Language Models
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) mitigates hallucination and knowledge staleness in large language models (LLMs) by injecting external knowledge into the context window, yet its effectiveness is rigidly constrained by attention dilution and inference cost. Existing knowledge-graph-enhanced methods follow a sequential “retrieve-then-compress” paradigm in which retrieval and compression are optimized independently, preventing the compressor from rectifying redundancy and noise introduced during retrieval and making it difficult to achieve globally efficient information allocation under a limited token budget. To address this paradigm-level limitation, we propose LOKG (LLM-Oriented Knowledge Graph), a high-information-density knowledge graph retrieval augmentation framework that uses token-level information density maximization as a shared design objective across schema compression, subgraph retrieval, and triple encoding. LOKG comprises three synergistic modules: Semantic Compression of Ontology Schema (SCOS) offline merges semantically overlapping relations by fusing normalized mutual information, Jaccard co-occurrence, and TransE embedding similarity under a conditional-entropy-based adaptive threshold; Topology-Aware Indexing and Multi-granularity Retrieval (TAIMR) computes topology-aware multi-hop path scores using relation-aware graph attention and node information gain, then applies late query–answer semantic re-ranking in the E5 space; Information-Theoretic Triple Compression (ITTC) formulates granularity assignment as a multiple-choice knapsack problem, adaptively allocating compact, balanced, or verbose representations to candidate triples to maximize injected information under the budget constraint. Experiments on four KGQA evaluation settings from three benchmark families (CWQ, WebQSP, PathQuestion-2hop, and PathQuestion-3hop) demonstrate that under a single-LLM-call constraint, LOKG achieves a superior accuracy–efficiency trade-off. Ablation studies further verify the orthogonality and synergy of the three modules. LOKG offers a transparent, auditable, and low-cost solution for knowledge graph retrieval-augmented generation under token budget constraints.

title: Beyond Explainability: A Clinically Constrained Counterfactual Machine Learning Framework for Malaria Diagnosis from Symptoms and Risk Factors
abstract: Diagnosis of malaria is challenging due to the complexity of clinical presentation, environmental risk factors and behavioural risk factors. Any machine learning (ML) technique can be used to help classify malaria; however, a high-accuracy model might not give much information on how the individual prediction was made. This research presents a clinically constrained counterfactual ML approach to classify malaria based on symptoms and risk factors. The accuracies, precisions, sensitivities, specificities, F1 scores, ROC-AUC and PR-AUC were used to compare the performance of Decision Tree, Random Forest and XGBoost classifiers. XGBoost gave the best overall performance with an accuracy of 83.06%, sensitivity of 87.16%, F1-score of 87.62%, ROC-AUC of 0.8830 and PR-AUC of 0.9387. Mosquito-bite exposure, bitter taste in the mouth, travelling to endemic areas, and severity of fever were some of the most important factors identified by feature-importance analysis. The chosen XGBoost model was then combined with a domain-driven counterfactual search method that safeguarded the immutable variables and limited the changes of the candidate variables based on clinical-consistency rules. The unconstrained baseline found no valid prediction-changing counterfactuals, while the constrained procedure found counterfactuals in 57.08% of the cases evaluated, with an average of 1.8237 modified features. The results demonstrate that domain-guided counterfactual search can deliver sparse prediction-change scenarios grounded in clinical knowledge, which are informative and easy to understand. The generated counterfactuals are meant to be an explanation of the model's decision boundary, not an assertion that changing a feature will cause a change in the patient's actual disease state. Before clinical application, the framework needs to be externally validated, have more robust resampling-based model validation and be compared to existing counterfactual-generation approaches.

title: Navigating Broken Data
abstract: One fundamental difference between AI for testing and regular non-player characters (NPCs) is that it must try to play the game as representatively as possible throughout production regardless of the current state of the game. During a project, the nav-mesh will at times be out of date and some areas or features might not yet be covered. In addition, test bots must often navigate in areas and deal with features, not meant for AI. This chapter will present some of the techniques and ideas used to make navigating unreliable data with input-driven test bots more robust.

title: Transparent Information Flow Modeling for Role-Aware AI Act Assessment
abstract: The European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act introduces a structured framework for governing high-risk AI systems, emphasizing transparency, risk management, and role-specific accountability. However, current assessment practices often rely on monolithic system views or disconnected checklists, limiting their ability to capture the socio-technical complexity of real-world deployments. We explore the use of the Information Flow Methodology (IFM), a modeling-based approach to AI Act compliance assessment. IFM represents decision systems -- whether algorithmic, human, or hybrid -- as networks of information sites and transformation channels, enabling structured analysis of how information, decisions, and responsibilities flow across organizational and technical boundaries. We apply IFM in a real-world case involving a recruitment support tool used by a public-sector organization, evaluating both the Provider's system and the Deployer's recruitment process. Our results demonstrate that IFM can serve as a scaffold to bridge both component-based and holistic perspectives, and how technical systems are situated within socio-technical contexts. In doing so, IFM supports transparency, identifies risk pathways, and enables alignment analysis between intended and actual use. We argue that such modeling provides a foundational tool for effective, context-sensitive AI governance and accountability -- offering capabilities beyond conventional checklist-based assessments.

title: Learning Deployable Causal Action Geometry under Temporal Non-Stationarity
abstract: Learning a response law for continuous decisions from observational time series is central to many real-world decision systems, yet temporal non-stationarity poses a fundamental challenge: as outcomes drift over time, naively pooled models can conflate action effects with shifting baselines and even reverse action rankings. Even when the one-step response is identifiable, unrestricted cross-time generalization remains fundamentally ill-posed. We therefore seek the part of the response that remains stable for decisions even when outcome levels do not. We propose deployable causal action geometry: the action-response shape that remains after anchoring away action-independent level shifts on a selected link scale and profiling out positive amplitude variation. Building on this target, we develop a two-stage orthogonal estimator that first obtains cross-fitted pilot estimates of anchored responses and then performs honest profiled selection over link, representation, and shape classes. The resulting estimator admits oracle guarantees for the restricted target and, under approximate persistence, produces decision rules that remain near optimal in future periods. Experiments on synthetic data and Dominick's support the proposed target and its transfer behavior. In a randomized Taobao A/B test, the deployed system improves GMV and purchase counts by \(1.16\%\) and \(1.70\%\).

title: Estimating the Causal Impact of Social Navigation Signals in Corridor Scenarios
abstract: Deploying robots in human-shared environments requires deciding not only how to navigate, but also when dedicated social signals are worth emitting. Classic observation-based inference can be misleading in such settings: confounding factors may bias the estimated relationship between a signal and the task outcome, leading to incorrect decisions. Causal inference provides a framework for disentangling these relationships by modelling the mechanisms linking observations, actions, and outcomes, and by estimating interventional effects after accounting for confounding paths. We study a human-robot interaction scenario in a corridor and use a causal model to estimate whether a social navigation signal causally improves transit success. We represent the interaction as a causal DAG involving robot action, pedestrian occupancy, available space, task outcome, and a controlled confounder (static obstacles). We compare the interventional estimate with the observational estimate obtained by conditioning only on the robot action, which does not explicitly model interventions. Our results show that accounting for confounding variables can reverse the conclusions drawn from naive observational analysis: the observational estimate wrongly suggests that the social signal is detrimental, whereas the causal estimate shows that it is beneficial. This discrepancy highlights how failing to account for confounding can lead to incorrect conclusions and demonstrates the importance of causal models for context-aware signalling decisions in social robot navigation.

title: All-St3R SLAM: Real-time RGB Dynamic SLAM with Pixel-wise Motion Masking
abstract: SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) is a core technology in autonomous systems that enables them to estimate their own position and build a map of unknown environments simultaneously. SLAM systems in dynamic environments are of great practical importance. However, existing dynamic SLAM approaches still have several limitations like over-removal and high computational costs. To address these limitations, we propose a real-time RGB Dynamic SLAM framework that precisely removes moving objects at the pixel level without relying on predefined labels or segmentation models. Our system combines pixel motion predicted by ego-motion using DUSt3R with point tracking from All-Tracker, removing only actually moving pixels by analyzing discrepancies between the two motion sources. Unlike object-level masking methods, our approach eliminates only currently moving regions, allowing temporarily static parts to be utilized for tracking. Operating at approximately 10 FPS, the system achieves real-time performance on standard 30 FPS video streams by subsampling every 3 frames. Relying solely on RGB inputs, this significantly improves upon state-of-the-art dense dynamic SLAM approaches (0.5-3 FPS), presenting a highly practical solution.

title: AI capability could grow explosively through research itself
abstract: AI research could do more than automate discovery: it could turn discoveries into the means of making increasingly capable AI. We propose that a potentially consequential part of this feedback lies in the formation, selective retention and revision of conditional research decisions—what to pursue, which evidence licenses a method, and when to abandon or reopen a route. If these decisions become reliably learnable, transferable and revisable, one investigation could enlarge the capacity of many subsequent investigations, including those that improve AI itself. Human researchers would be participants in this amplification, not merely fixed suppliers of labels: their judgment, skills, questions and division of responsibility could change with it. The strongest hypothesis is a transition from producing more research outputs to expanding the capability to generate further advances, with gains that compound rather than merely repeat. We distinguish this possibility from model improvement, parallel execution and amortized reuse, and identify observations that would weaken it. This Perspective reports no new experiment establishing the proposed mechanism or an observed capability explosion.

title: Python code for turn-pair analysis of AI feedback moves and learner regulation in WildChat-1M and LMSYS-Chat-1M
abstract: Python 3.10 code for relating assistant feedback moves to the learner's next turn in higher-education-related conversations from the public WildChat-1M and LMSYS-Chat-1M corpora. Run the scripts in numerical order; each file's header lists its commands, inputs and outputs. common.py: shared settings and helpers01_corpus.py: keyword funnel, language-model screening and its validation by a second model02_turn_coding.py: turn-level coding of assistant moves and learner stance with a fixed codebook prompt03_reliability.py: inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's and weighted kappa, bootstrap CIs)04_turn_pairs.py: assistant-to-learner turn pairs, transition tables, GEE models, move profiles by regulation level05_frames.py: language-model coding of each conversation's opening frame06_socratic_validation.py: blind validation of the Socratic-question code by two models07_socratic_sensitivity.py: GEE sensitivity models for Socratic questions No data or API keys are included. The corpora are downloaded from Hugging Face; model access is set through OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL, and file locations through DATA_DIR. Tested with Python 3.10.12, pandas 2.3.3, numpy 1.26.4, scipy 1.15.3, statsmodels 0.14.6, pyarrow 23.0.1 and openai 2.29.0.

title: Estimating Downward Shortwave Radiation over Complex Terrain: Synergizing Sentinel-2 Imagery and Topographic Data via Physics-Guided XGBoost
abstract: Downward shortwave radiation (DSR) varies strongly across mountain slopes, and products designed for horizontal surfaces may not resolve this variability. We estimated slope-parallel DSR at eight Saihanba sites using Sentinel-2 imagery, topography, atmospheric inputs, and BRDF-informed surface albedo. Both branches used XGBoost, with the clear-sky branch further incorporating a parameterized radiation anchor, bounded residual learning, and support-aware output correction. On the 2024 test set (n = 1451), the full framework achieved an RMSE of 92.60 W/m2, an NRMSE of 15.79% and an R2 of 0.897. Pooled leave-one-site-out validation across all 6096 samples yielded an RMSE of 113.68 W/m2. For horizontal-surface observations at 10 Heihe River Basin stations, NRMSE was 17.60%. Clear-sky estimates depended most on solar-incidence geometry, whereas top-of-atmosphere spectra dominated the cloudy-sky XGBoost model.

title: Raid Team Strategy (RTS): A Leader–Follower Metaheuristic with Team Merging for Multi-Basin Global Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes the Raid Team Strategy (RTS), a population-based metaheuristic inspired by the tactical organization of raid teams in search-and-attack operations. At each iteration, the best-ranked agents act as leaders and exploit their neighborhood through self-adaptive local search. In contrast, the remaining agents act as followers that are pulled toward the nearest leader along its direction of travel. The number of leaders is a fixed fraction of the population, while the number of teams that search separate regions changes during the run. Leaders that converge onto the same region are merged, and the weaker one is re-deployed at a random location; isolated but competitive followers are temporarily promoted to scouts, and stagnant followers are released to unexplored regions. RTS was evaluated under an equal budget of objective-function evaluations against ten methods, including the state-of-the-art L-SHADE, jSO and IPOP-CMA-ES and the deterministic DIRECT and DIRECT-L, on the CEC2017 (D = 10, 30, 50) and CEC2022 (D = 10, 20) suites with 51 independent runs, on the eight standard GKLS classes (800 randomly generated multi-extremal functions), and on six engineering design problems. RTS was significantly better than PSO, GWO, BA, and HHO on the CEC suites and statistically tied with SBOA, but it was clearly outperformed by L-SHADE, jSO, and IPOP-CMA-ES on the CEC suites and on the engineering problems. On the GKLS classes, RTS solved 638 of the 800 functions, compared with 260, 261, and 108 for L-SHADE, jSO, and IPOP-CMA-ES, and was exceeded only by the two DIRECT methods and, slightly, by HHO. An ablation study showed that the follower refinement and the focused probes are the components with a significant effect, and a sensitivity analysis showed that the results are robust to the parameter settings. The results position RTS as a method for landscapes with several separated basins rather than a fine local exploiter.

title: SchemaWeaver: Accelerating On-Device Mobile Agentic AI via Schema-Guided Parallel LLM Decoding
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) on mobile devices can act as agents that call external software tools to complete complex tasks, but the major challenge of supporting on-device mobile agentic AI with LLMs is the long latency of LLM tool calling on mobile devices. In particular, the decode phase is the main contributor of such long latency, but is hard to speed up on mobile processors as it is bound by memory bandwidth rather than compute power. To address this limitation, in this paper we present SchemaWeaver, a new on-device mobile agentic AI technique that enforces schema-guided parallel decoding in the decode phase of LLM tool calling, to reduce its latency by producing multiple tokens in each decode pass. SchemaWeaver can be generically applied to the LLM inference engine on mobile devices without involving any training efforts or changes on LLMs, and our experiment results on major mobile SoCs and LLM families show that SchemaWeaver can reduce the LLM tool calling latency by up to 3.9 times, compared to the competitive baselines.

title: Recovering from Pose-Selection Failures in Repeated Visual Localization
abstract: Repetitive structures can give an incorrect pose candidate more inlier support than an accurate one, causing visual localization to select it. History-Guided Pose Reselection (HPR) uses coarse position forecasts from up to five past localization outputs to distinguish well-separated current-query candidates. The best-fitting forecast proposes an alternative; HPR accepts it only if every well-fitting forecast is much closer to it than to the localizer's pose. HPR needs no odometry and returns the selected candidate unchanged, using prediction for selection rather than pose refinement. With one development-set threshold, HPR improves recall within 5 meters and 10 degrees in all 12 main configurations of Hierarchical Localization (HLoc), MASt3R-based pose generation, and JIST-based retrieval, losing successes on fewer than 0.4 percent of queries. On NAVER Gangnam B1, HPR corrects 97 HLoc failures and loses six successes; gains persist within 0.25 meters and 2 degrees on all three HLoc test sets. Median HPR runtime on HLoc candidates is below one millisecond, excluding pose generation. Recovery weakens under less frequent localization.

title: Device-to-protocol simulation of spectrally-resolved quantum photonic circuits
abstract: Predicting quantum-photonic circuit performance requires retaining source and device physics without making photon-counting calculations prohibitively expensive. Here we present PhoQuS, a framework that combines frequency-resolved source models, electromagnetic compact models and spatially correlated fabrication variation to simulate quantum photonic circuits. Covariance-Gram reduction after full-resolution Gaussian propagation lowers readout cost while retaining dominant spectral correlations. For continuous-variable state preparation, spectral reduction accelerates photon counting by 60.4-fold in an approximate Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill circuit. Frequency-resolved modeling guides the use of cascaded squeezing with temporal walk-off compensation, yielding 0.99 fidelity to the single-mode circuit reference and 0.98 conditional purity in lossless simulations. For discrete-variable state preparation, simulations of three-photon Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger circuits across a virtual wafer show that component robustness alone does not predict circuit fidelity, which depends jointly on source spectra, circuit architecture and control. PhoQuS connects device physics to protocol-level performance through a unified workflow that retains spectral detail while reducing readout cost.

title: Code and data for "Language models cite feature attributions accurately but rank borderline fraud cases no better than the classifier that produced them"
abstract: Language models increasingly review cases that fraud and intrusion classifiers cannot resolve. They are shown the classifier's feature attributions, numbers stating how much each input pushed the risk score up or down, and cite them as evidence, so their decisions look auditable. We tested whether such decisions depend on the evidence they cite, on five public datasets with eight language models (251,400 decisions, almost all near the alert threshold). Asked to copy cited values into structured fields, the models did so accurately: at least 99.8% matched the input. The attributions changed how often the models raised alerts, but averaged over datasets no model ranked cases better than the classifier (best area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.61 against 0.65), whereas a supervised model reading the same displayed numbers reached 0.90 and 0.96 on two datasets. In controlled displays, alert rates rose with the sum of the attributions, which near the threshold of a rare-event classifier is large and positive for every case. Presenting the same two debate arguments in reverse order changed alert rates by 1.7 to 20.9 percentage points in all eight models. Accurate citations therefore do not show that the evidence informed the decision. Every table, figure and number in the article regenerates from the records in this archive; see README.md. Row-level data of IEEE-CIS and UNSW-NB15 are not included, as their terms require; README.md explains how to rebuild them from the official sources.

title: Max Slate Einstein: bounded, evidence-aware educational character engine (research prototype)
abstract: Max Slate Einstein is an offline-first Python prototype of a bounded character engine for an Einstein-inspired educational avatar. It prefers a small, deterministic, policy-bounded response over unsupported elaboration. It separates persona policy, local source-linked knowledge records, session memory policy, routing and safety, and the response pipeline. Historical questions go to an evidence-conscious fallback, quote-attribution questions to a quote check (VERIFIED, DISPUTED or UNSOURCED), unsafe and professional-advice requests to refusal, and topics after 1955 or modern technology to an educator mode. Scope: an educational simulation. It does not claim that Albert Einstein speaks through it, nor sentience, autonomy or historical authenticity. It is not medical, legal, financial or safety-critical software, it uses no remote model, and long-term memory is disabled by default. Synthetic tests establish deterministic software behaviour only; no independent human, historical or security evaluation has been performed. Python 3.11-3.12, no runtime dependencies. 37 pytest tests plus ruff and compile checks run in GitHub Actions. License: MIT.

title: Dealer-Based (5,11) Threshold Quantum Secret Sharing Scheme: Design, Security, and Practical Considerations
abstract: We present DQ-(5,11), a dealer-based (5,11) threshold quantum secret sharing (QSS) scheme where any 5 of the 11 participants can find a dealer's secret and 4 or fewer get nothing about it. A key point is that, due to the Cleve-Gottesman-Lo no-cloning bound, there is only a (k,n) threshold scheme for any quantum secret if n < 2k. Since 11≥10, is a (5,11) quantity, the threshold scheme is impossible for quantum secrets, and in any (5,11) quantum secret sharing scheme there is a classical secret that is encrypted in a way that is protected by quantum communication. DQ-(5,11) is a combination of Shamir's polynomial sharing over GF13 and a single-qudit reconstruction in dimension d=13. Each of the five cooperating participants in DQ-(5,11) performs one phase operation with the share of the quantum secret and a zero-sum mask so that the intermediate states will not have any partial sum. Decoy qudits from two mutually unbiased bases detect eavesdropping, and a dealer-published commitment lets participants check the reconstructed value. We achieve correctness of all 462 subsets of the network, information-theoretic secrecy against coalitions of up to four insiders and a requirement for the success of intercept-resend attacks to be (d+1)/2d)m for m decoys (8.6×10-9) for m=30). We use numerical data to verify the deterministic reconstruction for all 2,310 runs and show the effect of depolarizing noise (79.1% success at 5% noise at each stage) and channel loss. Furthermore, we compare our orbital-angular-momentum and time-bin qudit model to Trojan-horse countermeasures and other schemes.

title: The artificial honey bee rearing optimization algorithm for hydraulic parameter optimization in multi-aquifer systems
abstract: Hydrological model calibration is crucial for seepage predictions, with parameter estimation a key challenge. Machine learning techniques have advanced for optimization in industries. Inspired by honey bee genetic manipulation, the Artificial Honey Bee Rearing Optimization (AHBRO) algorithm was tested on benchmark problems. Combined with the finite difference method, AHBRO was validated through pumping tests in Tianjin, China. Results show in low-dimensional spaces, AHBRO(WOA) outperforms models like EGA. For the Goldstein-Price function, AHBRO(WOA) achieved a fitness of 3.0000021, with a standard deviation of 1.15 × 10−5, better than EGA (fitness 3.0000145, standard deviation 4.36 × 10−4). In most high-dimensional spaces, BP-ANN improved AHBRO’s performance. In Tianjin tests, the estimated drawdown matched the measured values, showing excellent estimation ability with fewer function evaluations. Compared to EHBMO and EGA, AHBRO achieved results closer to the optimum, with an average NSE of 0.98. AHBRO offers an efficient, accurate solution for hydrological optimization, addressing convergence issues, with significant implications.

title: An optimized polar lights algorithm with SVM for early-stage esophageal cancer diagnosis
abstract: Esophageal cancer has high incidence and mortality rates, and early detection is important for improving outcomes. This study proposes bPLOAEA-SVM, which combines a binary form of the Polar Lights Optimizer (PLO) with Adaptive Elite Archive (PLOAEA) and a support vector machine (SVM) to select radiomic features from chest computed tomography images. PLOAEA was first assessed on the IEEE CEC 2020 and CEC 2022 benchmark suites, where it showed competitive optimization performance relative to the comparison algorithms. The clinical experiment included 1,720 single-center cases collected from 2010 to 2023 (974 healthy controls and 746 pathology-confirmed early-stage cases) and used repeated stratified 10-fold cross-validation. Across 10 runs, bPLOAEA-SVM achieved a mean accuracy of 92.203 %, recall of 89.774 %, specificity of 93.650 %, precision of 92.099 %, a Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.835, and an F1 score of 0.905. These internally validated results support the potential of PLOAEA-based feature selection for CT radiomics, while multicenter external validation is still required before clinical deployment.

title: World-T3: Test-Time Training as Persistent Memory for Real-Time Video World Models
abstract: Recent advances in video world models have enabled plausible interactive environments, yet long-horizon generation places a fundamental demand on visual memory: the previously observed world must remain consistent as the model continues to generate. Existing autoregressive approaches often implicitly rely on the generative model itself to retain such information, leading to spatial memory decay beyond the active context. We introduce World-T3, a camera-controlled video world model with a test-time training memory that consolidates past observations into dedicated model parameters. To robustly update this memory, we propose a recursive least-squares rule that incrementally absorbs novel visual features via online pose-keyed memory updates. Our TTT memory reads out previously observed scene features from the fast-weight state by camera pose, enabling consistent generation with constant storage and per-step computation regardless of rollout length. To facilitate real-time interactive generation with this robust memory, we further distill the autoregressive model into a few-step generator via dual-teacher distribution matching. On a long-horizon revisit benchmark, World-T3 raises revisit PSNR from 13.52 to 18.31 dB and reduces absolute rotation error from 3.344 to 1.075 relative to the strongest baseline on both metrics, while sustaining 20.6 FPS at 1280 x 704 on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU.

title: Comprehensive Workflow for Uncertainty-Aware Ionic Liquid Solvent Discovery
abstract: Designing synthesizable materials with targeted properties remains one of the central objectives in materials sciences. Ionic liquids (ILs) are well suited to this goal due to their "tunability", where physical and chemical properties can be precisely customized by modifying their molecular structure, specifically by varying the combination of cations and anions. At the same time, current data-driven property models for ionic liquids often degrade in scarce, noisy, and uneven data regimes, where measurements cover only a small fraction of chemical space and a limited range of thermodynamic conditions. This makes out-of-distribution screening brittle: even when point predictions look plausible, it is difficult to compare candidates consistently, quantify downstream implications, or trust rankings enough to guide molecular discovery. We present a property-prediction and optimal candidate selection workflow that treats data processing, deep learning modeling, and physics-based calculations as a coupled system, linking property prediction with uncertainty estimation and physics-based filtering. By tightening the link between predicted properties and the criteria used for down-selection, the workflow supports reliable out-of-distribution ranking and enables prioritization of previously untested ionic liquid candidates with favorable predicted trade-offs. We demonstrate the application of our workflow by designing novel ionic liquids for CO2 capture from flue gas, predicting their properties and selecting Pareto-optimal candidates based on CO2 solubility, IL viscosity and working capacity.

title: Audit tools of the trade: Automated Auditor Elicitation Can Be Sensitive to the Context the Auditor Is Given
abstract: Does providing additional context to automated AI auditors improve their effectiveness? Using the Petri tool to audit LLM coding agents, we test the impact of providing two types of resources (an external codebase and benchmark transcripts) to LLM auditors, across four auditor-target LLM pairs and three behaviours (harmful compliance, reward hacking, sycophancy). (1) External codebase: We provide the auditor LLM with a fixed, external open source codebase, which prior work finds improves the realism of synthetic audits. Providing this resource suppresses reward hacking in both auditor-target pairs whose baseline rate is above the floor (4.8 to 1.3 and 3.9 to 1.8 on Petri's default 1-10 scale); the remaining two pairs sit at the floor throughout. The suppression recurs in three of four pairs under a different scenario and resource bundle. (2) External benchmark transcripts: We provide the auditor with transcripts of the target's performance on benchmarks measuring similar behaviours, intended to inform the auditor about the target's behavioural patterns. Providing this resource raises reward hacking scores in all four pairs (from 1.7 to 6.1 in one case). However, subsequent experiments show that supplying only the related benchmark's abstract, without transcripts, also increases reward hacking, and the effect is absent under a different framing of the same behaviour. Overall, we find no consistent effect of either resource outside reward hacking, but we find substantial variability in judge-scored behaviour across conditions. Our results underscore the importance of careful piloting with tools such as Petri, as the measured rate of target behaviour is highly sensitive to configuration decisions. We hope our results inspire more research into the reliability and robustness of automated alignment auditing.

title: Towards Privacy-Preserving ASR: Speaker-Level Machine Unlearning
abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems are commonly designed to transcribe linguistic content independently of speaker identity. However, speaker-specific information can persist within the latent representations of ASR models, raising privacy concerns when training data includes sensitive individuals. While machine unlearning has been studied in several speech tasks, applying speaker unlearning to ASR remains challenging due to the strong entanglement of linguistic and speaker-related information in speech representations. In this work, we conduct a layer-wise analysis of Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) based ASR representations, revealing that speaker identity is primarily encoded in intermediate encoder layers. Based on this observation, we explore a feature-level unlearning strategy that targets these identity structures. Experiments on the VCTK corpus show that the proposed approach removes the influence of specific speakers while maintaining robust transcription performance.

title: AI in Action: Practical Applications for Startups
abstract: Susitikime dalyvavo daugiau nei 70 žmonių: startuolių kūrėjų, būsimų verslininkų ir fakulteto studentų. Tai antrasis ciklo susitikimas nuo jo pradžios pavasarį ir pirmasis naujajame sezone. Ciklo idėja paprasta: į fakultetą kviesti žmones, kurie technologijas taiko kasdieniame darbe, o ne kalba apie jas iš šalies. Buvo skaitomi du pranešimai : Dirbtinio intelekto demonstracija dar nėra veikiantis produktas ir DI agentas naudingas tik tada, kai darbą atlieka iki galo. Abu šio susitikimo pranešimai rėmėsi ta pačia prielaida — įspūdingas prototipas ir realiai veikiantis sprendimas yra du skirtingi dalykai. Startuoliams tai kasdienė problema: parodyti, ką technologija gali, yra paprasčiau nei ją paleisti taip, kad ji patikimai atliktų darbą ir kurtų vertę. Pirmąjį pranešimą „Building an AI Agent That Can Do Real Work” skaitė Marius Eitutis, „Ace Waves” vyriausiasis DI agentų inžinierius. Jis kalbėjo apie tai, kas skiria eksperimentinį dirbtinio intelekto agentą nuo tokio, kuriuo galima pasikliauti realioje darbo aplinkoje: kaip agentui apibrėžti užduotį, kaip jį sujungti su realiais duomenimis ir įrankiais, ir kur dažniausiai lūžta sprendimai, atrodę veikiantys demonstracijos metu. Klausytojams tai buvo praktinė medžiaga: ne apžvalga, kas yra DI agentai, o darbo su jais patirtis iš žmogaus, kuris juos kuria kasdien. Antrąjį pranešimą „From AI Demo to Business Value” pristatė dr. Mantas Lukauskas, „Hostinger” AI technologijų vadovas. Jo pranešimas tęsė tą pačią mintį iš verslo pusės: kaip įvertinti, ar dirbtinio intelekto sprendimas iš tikrųjų kuria vertę, kokius procesus jis realiai supaprastina ir kaip atskirti investiciją, kuri atsiperka, nuo tos, kuri lieka įspūdinga demonstracija. Pranešėjo patirtis technologijų bendrovėje leido kalbėti ne apie teorinius modelius, o apie sprendimus, priimamus veikiančiame versle.

title: flybrain-reservoir: fruit fly connectomes as echo state networks, against random wiring
abstract: Uses the wiring diagram of the adult male Drosophila central nervous system (166,700 neurons) as the recurrent network of an echo state network, drives it with market data, and compares it with control wirings that keep some of its statistics and scramble the rest. Replicated on the FlyWire female brain. Across the whole brain the fly's wiring remembers 8-11x less than random rewirings, and no wiring beats buy & hold.

title: Fault-Diagnosis-Aware Adaptive Policy Switching for Robust Map-Free Mobile Robot Navigation Under Sensor and Control Degradation
abstract: Heterogeneous sensor and control degradation can destabilize direct sensor-to-action navigation. This study presents a fault-diagnosis-aware adaptive policy-switching framework that combines a calibrated seven-class temporal health-state classifier with hysteretic routing among nominal, robust-fallback, and six fault-specialized proximal policy optimization (PPO) policies. Unlike monolithic robust reinforcement learning, the architecture makes the inferred degradation mode an explicit and auditable control variable and separates health-state inference from behavior selection. Across a large held-out simulation evaluation with three independently trained policy seeds, diagnosed switching improved the central severity-0.55 static benchmark and within-episode transition outcomes relative to robust PPO, while the broader severity sweep showed regime-dependent behavior. Diagnosed switching also retained an aggregate advantage under interaction-matched robust training. Mechanism controls showed that the gain depended on fault-specific specialist competence and correct fault-to-specialist correspondence rather than policy-bank capacity alone. Single-thread inference remained well below the 200 ms control interval. Within the evaluated simulation scope, the results support explicit online diagnosis and behaviorally matched policy selection as a practical strategy for robust map-free navigation under heterogeneous degradation.

title: State-backend-dependent fidelity of the CCZ gate on superconducting quantum computers
abstract: Abstract We present an experimental characterization of the three-qubit controlled-controlled-Z (CCZ) gate on IBM Quantum’s 127-qubit superconducting quantum computers, revealing state-backend-dependent performance variations. Using quantum state tomography (QST), we evaluate the gate’s output-state fidelity when applied to three algorithmically significant input states—the W state, the Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger (GHZ) state, and the uniform superposition state. Each state probes distinct aspects of the reconstructed state fidelity, the GHZ state tests coherence in maximally entangled systems, the W state reveals sensitivity to asymmetric errors, and the uniform superposition assesses basis-state-independent behavior. Experiments were conducted across three computational environments, noise-free simulation, noisy simulation, and actual hardware executions on three IBM Quantum computers, ibm_osaka , ibm_brisbane , and ibm_sherbrooke . State fidelities for the qasm_simulator remained above 99.2% for all input states. Noisy simulations yielded fidelities around 80–82%, while hardware results showed more significant degradation: 67.6% (GHZ), 59.0% (uniform superposition), and 50.3% (W)—highlighting the combined importance of state selection and hardware characteristics for reliable quantum computation. These results quantify the current performance gap between simulated and physical implementations of multi-qubit gates and provide a benchmark for error profiles relevant to near-term quantum algorithms

title: Multi-cepstral feature integration for audio deepfake detection under domain shift
abstract: Recent advances in speech synthesis and voice conversion technologies have enabled the creation of highly realistic audio deepfakes, posing significant challenges to biometric authentication, digital forensics, and misinformation detection. Although numerous countermeasures have been proposed, many existing approaches rely either on a single acoustic representation or on computationally intensive deep learning architectures, often exhibiting limited robustness when operating conditions differ from those observed during training. This paper investigates a lightweight and interpretable framework for audio deepfake detection based on the integration of multiple complementary cepstral representations. Specifically, Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Linear Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (LFCCs), Constant-Q Cepstral Coefficients (CQCCs), and Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (GFCCs) are jointly exploited to capture synthesis-related artifacts across different spectral resolutions and perceptual scales. The resulting feature representation is evaluated using conventional machine learning classifiers under strict speaker-independent protocols. Extensive experiments conducted on the FakeAVCelebV2 and ASVspoof2019 LA benchmarks, together with cross-dataset evaluations on the challenging In-The-Wild Audio (IWA) dataset, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework under both in-domain and out-of-domain conditions. Furthermore, a domain-stability analysis is introduced to investigate the contribution of individual acoustic descriptors to cross-dataset generalization and to identify features that remain robust across different data distributions. The obtained results demonstrate the effectiveness of integrating complementary cepstral representations for audio deepfake detection and highlight the importance of feature stability in improving cross-dataset generalization.

title: Learning Perceptual Geometry of Natural Odor Mixtures from LLM-Derived Descriptors
abstract: The relationship between odor chemistry and perception remains incompletely understood. Many existing studies focus on the perception of single molecules, whereas natural odors contain tens to hundreds of components, adding extra layer of complexity to percept formation. Here, we explore the relationship between molecular composition and perceived similarity in natural odor objects. We study this using a database of more than 1,200 volatile-compound-in-food mixtures containing more than 8,000 molecular components, and use large language models (LLMs) as a scalable surrogate for deriving mixture-level perceptual descriptions. We find that language-derived representations provide useful supervision for predicting held-out mixture similarities from molecular composition. The prediction was consistently strongest when perceptual targets were derived from chemosensory prompts than from other sensory prompts. Further, during the mixture-level training, we learned low-rank molecular embeddings that enabled better prediction of held-out mixture similarities than component-overlap metrics, even for mixture pairs with no shared molecules. Although no single-molecule labels were used during training, the learned molecular geometry showed significant alignment with the independent human odor-descriptor space. Finally, we explored the use of external molecular features in our mixture-similarity prediction task. These features showed modest zero-shot alignment with mixture-level perceptual similarity. They improved prediction under limited supervision but offered little additional predictive benefit with the full training set. Together, these results show that language-derived descriptions can provide scalable supervision for predicting the perceptual organization of complex natural mixtures, contributing to a quantitative understanding of how molecular composition gives rise to odor perception.

The prediction was consistently strongest when perceptual targets were derived from chemosensory prompts than from other sensory prompts. Further, during the mixture-level training, we learned low-rank molecular embeddings that enabled better prediction of held-out mixture similarities than component-overlap metrics, even for mixture pairs with no shared molecules. Although no single-molecule labels were used during training, the learned molecular geometry showed significant alignment with the independent human odor-descriptor space. Finally, we explored the use of external molecular features in our mixture-similarity prediction task. These features showed modest zero-shot alignment with mixture-level perceptual similarity. They improved prediction under limited supervision but offered little additional predictive benefit with the full training set. Together, these results show that language-derived descriptions can provide scalable supervision for predicting the perceptual organization of complex natural mixtures, contributing to a quantitative understanding of how molecular composition gives rise to odor perception.

title: ConDenseDrive: Knowledge-Dense, Token-Sparse Visual Encoder for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
abstract: End-to-end driving requires rich spatiotemporal representations to support scene understanding and trajectory planning under strict latency constraints. However, most systems initialize their visual encoders from generic image pretraining and densely process all patch tokens for each camera view and input frame, limiting both representation quality and inference efficiency. To address these challenges, we present ConDenseDrive, a knowledge-dense and token-sparse visual encoder for end-to-end autonomous driving. Our three-stage framework first makes the encoder knowledge-dense by distilling complementary visual, semantic, and geometric knowledge from three vision foundation models. It then adapts the distilled encoder to multi-frame end-to-end driving and integrates spatiotemporal context into register tokens for planning. Finally, it makes the encoder token-sparse by applying register-guided token compression, reducing redundant patch computation and yielding a 2.0$\times$ speedup while improving planning performance. ConDenseDrive achieves 94.5 PDMS on NAVSIM v1 and 90.8 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, and reaches 37.4 HD-Score in zero-shot evaluation on HUGSIM. Extensive experiments and qualitative analyses demonstrate that visual encoder design provides an effective route to reliable and efficient end-to-end driving.

title: Language2Drive: Do Vision-Language-Action Models Really Follow the Instructions in Autonomous Driving?
abstract: Recent Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models increasingly use natural-language instructions to condition autonomous driving behavior. Yet existing closed-loop benchmarks primarily measure route completion, safety, and rule compliance, leaving a fundamental question unresolved: does language actually determine which feasible behavior the vehicle executes? A trajectory may be safe and successful while still violating or even ignoring the passenger's instruction. To address this, we introduce \ltd, a benchmark designed to directly test this capability. Its key evaluation unit, the paired counterfactual unit (PCU), holds the initial driving scene fixed while changing only the instruction. This design enables us to distinguish isolated instruction success from counterfactual paired success across four instruction-following scopes. To test whether this distinction persists across evaluation regimes, we instantiate Language2Drive in complementary closed-loop CARLA simulation, reconstructed real-world scenes, and open-loop driving benchmarks, including our released CARLA-Language2Drive simulator with purpose-built maps. Evaluating representative driving VLAs across these settings reveals a striking mismatch between strong driving competence and weak language control: 93.2% of successful rollouts do not have a successful counterpart under the alternative feasible instruction. This failure is dominated by one-sided completion, where a model repeatedly executes one preferred behavior but fails when the same scene requires the counterfactual alternative. These results expose two fundamental limitations of current evaluation: isolated success and driving scores, which are widely used by conventional driving benchmarks, can substantially overstate language-following capability, while current driving VLAs themselves lack reliable instruction following under matched counterfactual tests.

title: Large Language Model Assisted Transportation Planning through a Differentiable User Equilibrium Layer
abstract: Transportation planning has traditionally required substantial expertise in network modeling, traffic assignment, and optimization. As a result, strategic analyses such as network design, capacity expansion, and model calibration remain inaccessible to non-expert decision makers. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) provide an opportunity to bridge this gap by enabling natural-language interaction with complex transportation planning tools. However, existing LLM-based systems primarily serve as interfaces to simulation software and lack the ability to efficiently search, evaluate, and optimize transportation solutions. This study proposes an integrated human-AI transportation planning framework that combines a large language model, a model context protocol (MCP) interface, an open-source transportation planning engine (AequilibraE), and a differentiable user equilibrium (UE) assignment layer. The framework allows non-expert users to execute network analyses and improve solutions for optimization. A differentiable UE layer is developed by directly differentiating the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions of the Beckmann traffic assignment problem. The proposed framework is demonstrated through two representative planning tasks: calibration of travel time functions from observed traffic counts and network design under budget constraints. The examples illustrate how differentiable transportation models and LLM agents can jointly democratize transportation planning and substantially reduce barriers between domain expertise and transportation decision making.
